Keywords: slow, outlook, fixes, –, it, follow, is, running
Summary: IT, procedure, Outlook, performance, troubleshooting.
detail:
1. Outlook Data File Issues (Corrupted or Large OST/PST)
Cause: Outlook files can become corrupted or too large over time.
How to Check:
Go to File > Account Settings > Data Files and check the size of the OST/PST file.
Run ScanPST.exe to repair the file.
Solution:
Compact the file: File > Account Settings > Data Files > Settings > Compact Now.
Rebuild the OST file: Rename the old OST and let Outlook recreate it.

2. Add-Ins Causing Delays
Cause: Problematic or unnecessary Outlook add-ins can slow performance.
How to Check:
Go to File > Options > Add-ins > Manage COM Add-ins > Go.
Disable all add-ins and test Outlook.
Solution:
Re-enable add-ins one by one to identify the culprit.

3. Search Indexing Issues
Cause: Outlook search indexing can become corrupted or incomplete.
How to Check:
In Outlook, click the Search box and select Indexing Status.
Check if indexing is stuck or incomplete.
Solution:
Rebuild the index:
Go to Control Panel > Indexing Options > Advanced > Rebuild.

4. Outlook Profile Corruption
Cause: User profile corruption can cause Outlook to lag.
How to Check:
Test Outlook with a new profile:
Go to Control Panel > Mail > Show Profiles > Add.
Create a new profile and set it as default.
Solution: Use the new profile to check if the issue resolves.

5. Windows or Office Updates Causing Issues
Cause: Recent updates can sometimes cause compatibility issues.
How to Check:
Go to File > Office Account > Update Options > View Updates.
Check Windows Update history: Settings > Update & Security > View Update History.
Solution:
Roll back problematic updates or run Quick Repair:
Go to Control Panel > Programs > Microsoft Office > Modify > Quick Repair.

6. Outlook Cache Issues
Cause: Cached Exchange Mode files can sometimes slow performance.
How to Check:
Disable Cached Exchange Mode:
Go to File > Account Settings > Account Settings > More Settings > Advanced > Uncheck Cached Exchange Mode.
Solution: Restart Outlook, test performance, then re-enable Cached Exchange Mode.

7. Antivirus Scanning Outlook
Cause: Antivirus programs can scan Outlook emails and slow it down.
How to Check:
Temporarily disable the antivirus and test Outlook.
Solution: Add Outlook processes to the antivirus exclusion list.

8. System Resource Issues
Cause: Low memory, CPU, or disk space may affect Outlook.
How to Check:
Open Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc) to monitor CPU, RAM, and disk usage.
Check free space on the C: drive.
Solution: Free up disk space and restart the computer.

Quick Steps to Start With:
Disable all Add-Ins and restart Outlook.
Repair the OST/PST file using ScanPST.exe.
Test Outlook in Safe Mode: Press Win + R, type outlook.exe /safe, and hit Enter.
Check Windows/Office Updates and apply any pending updates.
Rebuild the Outlook search index.

detail:
The issue 
Having spreadsheets in two different windows can make some Excel tasks easier. the main benefits are
while Excel is busy recalculating one of your workbooks, you can continue working on another.
you can use the back button to only go back within the sheet you are looking at and not skip to other sheets and undo things on those sheets.

the problem however is 
that this is not default excel functioning and would require sensitive registry editing to make the default
if you were to make this default for some users but not all it might cause issues making excel set up this way function differently to excel in other areas of the company, this would compromise a very important basic assumption that the excel file you send to another person will behave as it does on your computer.
if we were to make it default for everyone then it might compromise how some people work between sheets.

The solution
From the above - we want a temporary user specific solution. Some options are below.

Recent file method
Steps
If you have recently used the file
Right-click the Excel icon on the taskbar.
Hold down the Alt key and left-click Excel in the menu.
/

start it in a new instance
/

Pros to this method : easy and natural IF it is a recent file
Cons to this method : if it is not a recent file you would have to open it then close it (to make it a recent file) then reopen it again.

Bat file method
Preparation 
Save this file to your desktop EMBED Package 
Steps 
drag a new excel file onto it
/
This will open in a new session   no messagebox.

Pros to this method   simple
Cons to this method   desktop isn t always visible, may be hard to remember

Standard method
Steps
In File Explorer, browse for the target file.
Double click the file (as you normally do to open it) and immediately after that press and hold the Alt key. You need to be reasonably fast.
Keep holding Alt until the new instance dialog box pops up.
Click Yes to confirm that you want to start a new instance.
/
Pros to this method   standard functionality
Cons to this method   requires some timing

Shortcut method
Preparation
 Save this shortcut to your computer
Q:\Information Technology\Tools\EXCEL new window.lnk
Steps

When you want to open a new session use this short cut
then in that session browse to open the file
Pros to this method   standard functionality
Cons to this method   users may instinctively double click before thinking to drag, also need to remember to open a browser to see the bat file (or use the desktop). Slower.

Data Layout:

/
Note you can see this format is line the one if you export budgets
/
Except for these - The second to last column we will add a sum for each row (and column) and a target value (we will work this out from  the instructions we have been given) and a ratio (of the target to the sum)
Adjustment of Totals:
Correct the totals for stock groups and months to desired amounts. This is achieved by calculating the factor needed to adjust the current totals to target figures, and then applying this factor across the relevant rows or columns. Use this to correct targets form the sum to the amount required.
Handling Mismatched Categories:
If product categories provided do not match existing stock groups, you may need to handle them as a group. Select the range (for example maybe the  rest  category) and see how much that is then determine the amount you need to multiply it by to get the total you want and then do that multiplication. 
Continue to adjust multiple stock group rows to align with the provided categories until you have the totals that you want.
Make sure the sum of the rows equals the sum f the columns or the next step wont work.
Iterative Spreading:
You can now repeat the adjustment process multiple times for the entire table alternating by row and by column, this must be done a few times as redistributing totals in one direction can affect the totals in another.
I would select the entire column of ratios then paste special over the entire table with the below settings, then repeat for rows, and then do both a few times always ending in copying the rows over the table  so month totals are exactly right.

Summary: Health and safety manual outlining core workplace policies and practices. Worksite Hazard and Incident Management:1.
detail:
Worksite Hazard and Incident Management:
1. The premises of Firstflex are to be inspected on a monthly basis for any hazards, including, but not limited to: potential trip, slip and fall hazards, electrical, height safety and fire compliance including egresses and exits [See Appendix 13   Site Inspection Form]
2. Aisle Inspection to be carried out in the warehouse every Wednesday with inspection report emailed to all H&S   team members.
3. Prior to commencement of any significant work, hazards and potential hazards are discussed, with procedures being adopted and documented to mitigate these hazards.  This includes:
3.1. Staff being advised of all safety requirements.  These will include any that are specific to a particular site.
3.2. Staff being advised of all personal protective equipment and clothing requirements.
3.3. Personal protective equipment is provided to all employees and all employees are trained in its use.
4. Updates on safety requirements for all mechanical engineering staff, are carried out at  toolbox meetings  which are conducted prior to work starting and as issues arise.
5. Staff, contractors and other visitors are briefed and also alerted to site specific hazards and to general safety requirements through visual signage erected on site.
6. Areas where machinery is being used should be restricted to authorised personnel only.  Appropriate signage and hazard tape used where appropriate.
7. Visitors to the workshop must wear a high visibility vest.

Health & Safety Meetings
Health & Safety team meetings are held bi-monthly.   Meetings are compulsory for key staff and a minimum of one management representative must be present.  The meeting agenda includes:
O' Updates to Firstflex s Health & Safety policies and procedures,
O' Accident incident review,
O' Hazard Management, including site specific issues,
O' Key issues from toolbox meetings,
O' Re-Occurring Incidents,
O' Off-site issues if any; and
O' Staff concerns and suggestions in regard to health & safety.
Procedures will be amended and manual documentation will be updated where required as a result of outcomes of the monthly health & safety meetings.
Staff are further notified through a group meeting or hard copy memo of any changes or updates to Firstflex Cables Health & Safety policies and procedures and associated changes to Health & Safety documentation.
Toolbox Meetings
Health & safety is also an important part of onsite toolbox meetings.  At toolbox meetings a review of accidents/ incidents, hazards and general staff concerns are covered.  In the same manner as above, procedures are amended and manual documentation is updated where required.
Toolbox meetings can be a regular scheduled occurrence if the industry or business requires this approach or a more informal process (in addition to the scheduled health & safety meeting) used whenever the team discusses health & safety issues.
The specific function of the toolbox meeting is to assist with health & safety specific to the current work that team members are working on.  During this meeting, the team will review, plan and implement and actions relating to health & safety including, but not limited to the following:
O' Accidents/ incidents, including serious harm, near misses, and associated trends
O' Regular site inspections,
O' Hazard assessments, including new hazards and a review of the hazard register,
O' Personal protective equipment,
O' Contractor work, including any new contractors that have come onto site,
O' Any other issues arising from the work being performed, and
O' Health & Safety training where required,
O' Progress of work and specific tasks,
O' Health & Safety, specifically hazards, accidents/ incidents and PPE requirements; and
O' Mitigation of risks identified in the above
All of the above is recorded in the toolbox meeting minutes (Appendix 6.1) and any information that is relevant to either the site or staff in general, is communicated via general memorandum or staff email.  Appropriate action is taken immediately if required and review takes place at the next toolbox or health & safety meeting.
Key issues from toolbox meetings should be reported in the next Health & Safety Meeting.
Refer to Firstflex Health and Safety Manual for full duties

Technical Explanation of the Pricing Sheets
What Does It Do?
The 4-supplier template takes the pricing sheets from the suppliers and uses them to update Pronto according to certain rules.
Formatting the Data for Pronto
First, it creates a format that matches the raw data so the results sheet is, in essence, a copy of that raw data, ready to upload back into the same screen.
This is seen in column A, which directly pulls the data:
='raw pronto'!A2
Handling Blank Values
Some columns need to return blanks instead of zeros:
=IF('raw pronto'!B2=0,"",'raw pronto'!B2)
Supplier 1 Code Handling for X Articles
Any X article should use the supplier of the normal article. X codes represent the same product but are separated to avoid interfering with reordering.
=IF(IF(LEFT(A2,1)="X",'raw pronto'!J2,VLOOKUP(MID(A2,1,99),'raw pronto'!A:J,10,FALSE))=0,"",IF(LEFT(A2,1)="X",'raw pronto'!J2,VLOOKUP(MID(A2,1,99),'raw pronto'!A:J,10,FALSE)))
Looking Up the Supplier and Standardizing X or ASSY Articles
The supplier is identified, and then the article is found on the vendor sheets. If it is an X article or an ASSY article, the standard (non-X) article is found.
If this formula is too complex, a helper worksheet could be used to combine data from each vendor, along with a helper column that assigns the standard article for every item.
=LET(
    lookupValue,
    IF(
        LEFT($A2,1)="X", RIGHT($A2, LEN($A2) - 1),
        IF(RIGHT($A2,4)="ASSY", LEFT($A2, LEN($A2) - 4), $A2)
    ),
    result,
    IF(
        J2="HENRYCAB", IF(COUNTIF('raw HC'!$A:$A, lookupValue) > 0, VLOOKUP(lookupValue, 'raw HC'!$A:$M, 11, FALSE), 0),
        IF(
            J2="RAMRATNA", IF(COUNTIF('raw RR'!$A:$A, lookupValue) > 0, VLOOKUP(lookupValue, 'raw RR'!$A:$N, 11, FALSE), 0),
            IF(
                J2="DOMINION", IF(COUNTIF('raw DC'!$A:$A, lookupValue) > 0, VLOOKUP(lookupValue, 'raw DC'!$A:$Z, 9, FALSE), 0),
                IF(
                    J2="TKDKABEL", IF(COUNTIF('raw TKD'!$A:$A, lookupValue) > 0, VLOOKUP(lookupValue, 'raw TKD'!$A:$O, 9, FALSE)/1000, 0),
                    VLOOKUP($A2, 'raw pronto'!$A:$O, 15, FALSE)
                )
            )
        )
    ),
    IFERROR(ROUND(result, 4), 0)
)

This process repeats for Supplier 2 and Supplier 3.
Looking Up TKD Part Numbers
On the TKD sheet, the system looks up internal part numbers on the TKD codes sheet. This is a query that can be refreshed.
=IFERROR(VLOOKUP([@[TKD Part Number (txt)]]&"",'TKD codes'!E:F,2,FALSE),"")
Formatting Codes to Match TKD's Format
The system converts internal codes to match the TKD format by trimming and removing unnecessary parts:
=LEFT(B2, FIND(" ", B2 & " ") - 1)
Ensuring internal codes are properly trimmed:
=TRIM([@[stock_code]])

It looks up rebate from the rebate sheet
=IFERROR(VLOOKUP(C3,Rebate!A:B,2,FALSE),"")
Column Y will have the final results in it but it needs to initially present us with the current listed prices so it gives us prices from the pronto sheet(data) and if it is an x article it looks up the non x articles data (as that wouldn t have list proices)
=IFERROR(IF(AND(LEFT(A4,1)="X",Data!Y3=0),XLOOKUP(MID(A4,2,99)&W4,Data!A:A&Data!W:W,Data!$Y:$Y,"",0),Data!Y3),0)

Now BB onwards we aggregate stock by the products stock brand / generic
BB looks up the generic
=IFERROR(VLOOKUP(A2,generics!$C:$D,2,FALSE),A2)
We do the sum if based on the generic to give the numbers that will calculate aversge costs
=IFERROR(IF(BB5="","",SUMIF(BB:BB,BB5,BC:BC)),"")
Calculate the cost average
=IFERROR(IF(LEFT(A5,1)="X",IF(BB4=BB5,BF4,IFERROR(INDEX(BD:BD,MATCH(MID(A5,2,99),A:A,FALSE))/INDEX(BE:BE,MATCH(MID(A5,2,99),A:A,FALSE)),"")),IF(BB4=BB5,BF4,IFERROR(BD5/BE5,""))),"")
Now we calculate price tiers based on the minimum margin (AR) the cost (BF) and slowly increasing it and defaulting to the replacement if there is nothing with tiers based on how many price steps there are (BN)

=IFERROR($BF6/(1-($AR6)/100),IFERROR(K6/(1-($AR6)/100),""))
=IFERROR($BF4/(1-($AR4+2*$BN4)/100),IFERROR(K4/(1-($AR4+2*$BN4)/100),""))

I need to know the no of unpublished items so I know how many teirs are unpublished, unpublished is over 4999
=IF(AND(A2=A1,D2=D1,W1>4999),BW1,IF(W2>4999,COUNTIFS($A:$A,A2,$D:$D,D2)-BV2+1,""))
I assign a minimum grade (looking it up on the minimum price sheet
=IFERROR(VLOOKUP(CG2,'Minimum Price'!$A$1:$B$12,2,FALSE),"")
And calculate a floor for the product based on preplacement cost
=IFERROR(K2*1/(1-VLOOKUP(CG2,'Minimum Price'!$A$1:$B$35,2,FALSE)),"")
And calculate a max of that to get it at the generic level
=IF(BB2="","",MAXIFS($CD$2:$CD$20000,$BB$2:$BB$20000,BB2))
And put it all together in the final price
=IFERROR(ROUND(IF(Y2+0=0,"",IF(BO2=0,Y2,IF(BW2="",Y2,MAX(MIN(CE2,IF(A2=A1,CC1,Y2)),IF(CA2="N",OFFSET(BO2,0,COUNTIFS($A:$A,A2,$D:$D,D2)-BV2),IF(AND(CC1<BO2,A2=A1,D2=D1),CC1,CB2)))))),2),"")

That value is them pasted to the Y column and we upload the price file

Make up the electrician pack (ELEPAC) using the following items as per the photo: BAG9, NEUSTA, SCR820PP x 4, SCR812MP X 2

Remove the protective strip from the acrylic window and carfully place in a pile, so you don t scratch them

Apply adhesive uniformly on the inside of the lid around the window space.

Stack the glued lids into piles of 25, separating the lids by placing the wooden boards between the lids.

Place 50kg of weight on top of each stack within 45 mins of completing a stack.

Leave lids for 24 hours to cure.

Screw 2 x 10g x 5/8 screws into the hole on the bottom of the meter box base.

Stick an Electrex label on the bottom inside centre of the metre box base.

Place the MGBFK (Flashing Kit) inside the assembled meter box base

Place the MGBLID (Meter Box Lid) upside down on top of the MGB base

Slide the assembled meter box base and lid into the MGB carton and tape the carton shut.

Mark the center of the lid.
	Note: Cable entry panel must be at the bottom of box & door hinges on left hand side.

Follow the instructions on the label and drill the holes. Cut the centre hole to 37mm, (this size is required so the clips to secure the screws will slip far enough back from the hole).
Take off the instruction label and clean the surface of the lid.

Put changeover switch label on the center
Take the cover off the handle, see instruction sheet included with handle.
Affix the handle to the lid with the 4 screws that come with the handle.

Put the cover back on the handle.

Unscrew the mounting plate and take it out of the box
Mark the center of the plate

Put the changeover switch mech vertically on the plate and line up the black switch connector with the center and mark the screw holes with a pen.
Drill the screw mark with a 3.5mm drill bit.
Tap the holes with 4mm.
Drill hole at bottom right corner with 6mm drill bit for the earth wire.
Secure the mech using screw SCRM416PP.
For earth wire mounting hole, affix screw SCRM620PPB from the bottom of plate, then use 2 x WASHM6B and 2 x NUTM6B.

Put 570.0125 on the right hand side of the box 15mm from the top.
Mark all of the screw holes.
Drill holes with 5mm drill bit.
Drill a hole approx. 5mm below the center of circle on 570.0125.
Temporarily affix 570.0125 and mark the box through the drill hole.
Use the 63mm hole cutter to drill a hole through the box.
Use the 63mm hole cutter to drill a hole through the 570.0125.
Cut the bottom part of the cable gland off.
Put gland on and tighten locknut from the inside of the box.
Affix 570.0125 and screw on cut down gland top.

Measure the distance from the 248.12597 inlet end of the 570.0125 through to the anchor point for the earth wire on the mounting plate inside the box. Cut1 piece of CW0025.0G/YASSY (25mm earth wire).  
Strip insulation for the CVORTER25 based on the measurement on the back of the 248.12597 inlet

Attach a CORTER25 to one end and a LUG256 to the other end using the CABAC K06 crimper

Using the yellow/green heat shrink, cover both ends where the CORTER25 and LUG256 meet the wire.
Attach the earth wire to both the inlet plug and the mounting plate.
Measure the distance from the plug end of the 570.0125 inlet through to the switch mech inside the box and cut 4 pieces of BFX025BKASSY (25mm cable)
Attach a CORTER25 to each end of the 4 cables using the CABAC K06 crimper.
Using the black heat shrink, cover both ends of one cable where the CORTER2 5meets the cable.
Repeat step 32 with the other heat shrink colours so you have 1 x black, 1 x red, 1 x blue and 1 x white.
Attach each cable in turn to both the inlet plug and the switch mech. 
Note: cut a small section off the end of the CORTER25 that is to attach to the switch. This is to prevent any part of the CORTER showing outside of the switch.
As per the photo on the next page, measure and cut 4 x BFX025/BKASSY to connect to each section of the switch mech.
Attach 1 x CORTER25 to one end and 1 x FINDER 25 to the other end of each of the four cables.
Using the black heat shrink, cover both ends of 1 cable where the CORTER25 and FINDER25 meet the cable.
Repeat step 37 with the other heat shrink colours so you have 1 x black, 1 x red, 1 x blue and 1 x white.
Attach each cable in turn to both sections of the switch.
Note: Cut a small section off the end of both the CORTER25 and the FINDER25. This is to prevent any part of them showing outside of the switch.
Cut the handle shaft to 135mm and attach to switch.
Measure and cut CW006.0G/YASSY earth wire to run from the mounting point at the top right hand corner of the lid to the mounting point on the top left corner of the box.
Attach LUG66 to each end of the cable and cover where they join the cable with heat shrink.
Remove mounting point covers, curl the wire to form a spring shape and attach end using WASHM6B and NUTM6B as shown in the photo.

Choose the correct label for the outlet position on ST box
Wire the block according to outlet position.
Shaft length is 135mm

detail:
Operational Features
The ET30 meter is a 30amp coin or token operated electronic timer. Is provides secure, reliable and affordable timing metering solutions for switching up to 30 amps. Standard features include credit save facility, resettable and non-resettable coin counter, dual or single coin operation and the time period may be set in minutes and seconds or hours and minutes. An optional override key is available.

Main features
The 4 digit 7 segment display, in conjunction with the hidden programming buttons is used to program the ET30, as well as showing the time remaining and mode of operation (figure 4)
The coin entry inserts tokens or coins.
The optional key override switch turns the timer output on permanently.
Access for wiring is via the cover lock (see Wiring).
Cash box holding 100 coins.
Hidden programming buttons (Programming credit, page 3)

Preparation for programming
Unlock and remove cash drawer (this needs to be left out while programming)
Unlock the front cover of the meter and lift upwards slightly and away from the wall bracket (see Figure 2).  
Unplug the cover ribbon cable lead from the wall bracket and remove cover.
For Coin Operation see below, for Token Operation go to Wiring section

Coin Operation
Unscrew clear plastic cover and remove, (2 screws) 
Unscrew black plastic cover and remove, (2 screws)
Discard the short screw as it will no longer be required.

Remove L2 label and the small plastic strip behind it.  This can be discarded.
Remove the plastic guide rail.

Remove the token adaptor plate and replace with a coin adaptor plate, either ET30CK1.00 (for $1 coins) or ET30CK 50 (for 50cent coins).
Reassemble black plastic cover & clear plastic cover.  Note, no screw through the wiring label.

Wiring
Wire the unit as shown in Figure 3.
The meter can be connected to the supply via a cable fed through the hole in the back of the wall bracket.
Plug the ribbon cable from the front cover to the connector located in the wall bracket and fit the front cover onto the wall bracket, drop down slightly and lock into place.
Apply power.

Service Mode
The service mode consists of four settings split in to two functional areas:
Programming credit
Audit functions
To access service mode remove the coin box: 
Press and release button B (figure 4) to step to the desired setting number (St.01 to St.04). 
Simultaneously pressing and releasing both buttons A and B will step back to the previous setting. 
On reaching the required setting number press button A to enter desired values

Programming Credit
The credit functions allow the meter to be programmed for a fixed time session.
Press and release button B to step to the desired setting number.
When the required number is showing on the display, press button A to display the existing setting. Press and release button A to select the digit to be changed, then press and release button B to alter that digit.

Note
Coins and tokens are validated by two coin sensors.  
Coin sensor 1 (St.01) validates $1 coins, L2 and L4 tokens.  
Coin sensor 2 (St.02) validates 50 cent coins and L1 tokens.
St.01 Credit (Fixed Time) Per Coin 1: 
Sets the amount of credit given by coin sensor 1, set in HH.MM or MM.SS
St.02 01 Credit (Fixed Time) Per Coin 2: 
Sets the amount of credit given by coin sensor 2, set in HH.MM or MM.SS
Replacing the coin drawer will save the settings.

Content: Live Testing of 230V Electrical Products ProcedureScope: Testing 230V electrical products.Requirements:RCBO test rig (Test & Tag up to date)QUICKTEST rig2 People (1 Person must have previous testing experience) Details:First identify if the device needs live testing. Live Testing of 230V Electrical Products Procedure

Scope: Testing 230V electrical products.

Requirements:
RCBO test rig (Test & Tag up to date)
QUICKTEST rig
2 People (1 Person must have previous testing experience) 

Details:
First identify if the device needs live testing. If not, use an alternative method for instance the PAT tester
When live testing needs to be carried out, the buddy system detailed below needs to be followed.
2 people need to be present during a testing procedure
One being the tester the other being the observer
The observer s role is to limit any distractions directed towards the tester whilst in the middle of testing. They are also there to bring to the attention of the tester any potential hazard that may occur while carrying out testing
If testing starts to exceed 10 minutes, please advise the Electrical Production Manager ASAP
The observer and the tester are to report any NEAR MISS to the Electrical Production Manager immediately and fill out the appropriate forms

RCBO Testing Procedure

Check RCBO test rig for an up to date Test & Tag label and for any obvious damage
Connect white 3-pin 10A plug into a power outlet and switch it on

 /
 
 

Open the cover and switch the RCBO upwards to the ON position

 /
 
 

Press the TEST button on the RCBO and check that the RCBO switches back to the OFF position before continuing
 /
 
 

Check for any other potential hazards or damage to the product requiring a test before plugging it into one of the below sockets

 /
 
 

Switch the RCBO to the ON position to begin testing the product

 /
 
 
Proceed to test the live device with caution and isolate the product if found to be faulty

Testing with live leads (QUICKTEST)
Details:
When testing with live leads always use the QUICKTEST isolation unit
The QUICKTEST unit can be plugged into the above RCBO jig (in series) to add an extra layer of protection while testing
The QUICKTEST will liven the 3 output terminals when the black lid is closed

QUICKTEST Testing Procedure

Plug the power inlet for METREL into the RCBO test rig

  EMBED PBrush 
 
 

Plug the white QUICKTEST plug into the METREL tester

 /
 
 

Connect the live lead to the item to be tested

 /
  EMBED PBrush 
 
 

 
 
 

Open up the QUICKTEST unit and connect your live lead to the 3 terminals as below. Press the far end of the coloured terminal to open it up
 /
 
 

 

	Example of CARSUPBX wired up for testing
 /
 
 

After all connections are made close the lid on the QUICKTEST unit and proceed with your live testing as per the standard testing procedure

When testing multiple products disconnect the QUICKTEST unit from the METREL before disconnecting from the product

After the test is complete, turn off power at the wall, open the QUICKTEST unit to disconnect the circuit, then remove the live lead from the item under test

Product code: PILLAR various options
Description: Pillar power supply stand

 
 ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS
There are various option for theses stands where a light and or KWH meters may be added. 
Check paint finish on pillar stand before proceeding.

If the PP1490x220 panel is supplied without the switch window cut out use the template by positioning on to the film protected side of the panel and marking the outline and holes.
If required, due to the number of switches / KWH meters required, a second switch window hole can be cut below the first using the same template.

 /
 
 
Cut out the window hole(s) with a craft knife.  Drill out the holes to 5mm.
Pick best side of the pillar stand, use this as the front.

Measure 300mm up from the base plate and on the right hand side mark the inside of both front and back channels.  This is where the din rail will affix.

 /
 
 
Cut down a din rail to 130mm in such a way as to leave a part slot each side.  Refer to drawing.

 
 EMBED PBrush 
 
 
Hold the din rail in position and drill a 3mm hole each side.
Tap these holes to take a 4mm screw.
Affix with a screw and 2 washers per hole.

 /
 
 

Glue an end plate to one CSTSN6U terminal, then attach 3 to this din rail.
Attach a CA702 terminal stop to each side.  Attach a CSTSPC1-1 cap over the terminals.
Print a label with L  N  E and affix to above the terminals.
Peel back the protective film from the edges on the face panel.
Carefully slide down the channels.

Assemble the 8 way window frame(s).
Attach the switches to the frame din rail(s).
Attach one CSTSN6U terminal to either side of switches, (only on bottom din rail if two rails being used).
Wire up top connections of the switches (neutral from the top position of the terminal).
If KWH meters are required they can be wired up too. Refer to AS250 CARSUPBX procedure wiring diagram.
If a light is required place the lid in position and mark approx. 25mm down from the bottom edge of the lid and centered left to right on the wall of the pillar.
Hold switch din rail(s) temporarily in position and measure to the outlet positions for the live, neutral and earth wires (earth from top position of terminal).  Cut the required wires.
 /
Example of Pillar 2
 
 
Measure from the bottom position on the neutral terminal, bottom of the main switch and bottom position on the earth terminal down to the bottom din rail terminals. Cut required wires, using 2.5mm cable for single outlet and 4mm for all other option.
Curl a section of 2.5mm earth wire then run it from the top earth terminal to the closest outlet mounting hole to determine required length. 
Connect all wires to their corresponding positions on the switches and top terminals, as per photo.
Using a small grinding stone attachment clean the paint from around the outlet mounting hole chosen for the frame earthing contact point. 
If a light is required drill through the side of the pillar at the marked position. 
Attach the photo cell.
Attach the din frame(s) and the window(s) to the face panel.
Peel back the protective film from the edges of the face panel and side down into the pillar channels.
If a light is required connect the photo cell to the light switch.

Drill out the screw holes in the outlets to 5mm.
Connect wires to outlets and mount to the pillar including the frame earthing wire.
Note, the earthing wire requires a brass washer, lock washer and brass nut to secure it.

  EMBED PBrush 
 
 

TERMINAL TO SWITCH / TOP TERMINALS

For units with 2 or less outlets use 4mm wire.
For units with 3 or more outlets use 6mm wire.
Secure the wires to the bottom terminals.
Attach terminal ID label.
Connect the other ends of the wires to their corresponding positions.

 /
 /
Example of Pillar 2
 
 Affix 2 electrical warning labels, one just above the bottom terminals and one just below the switch gear.
Secure the wires with cable ties.
 
 
 

Cut a section of PVC to fit in the channels across both sides at the top of the pillar.
Slip in to channels, hold in place then drill through channels and into PVC for 4mm screw fixing.
Using the hole in the pillar drill through these pieces of PVC each side.
Cut a section of PVC to bridge across the top of the fixed PVC sections.  Glue in place.
 /
 
 

If a light is required affix the transformer and LED light strip and connect all required wires.
Temporarily place the lid on top of the pillar.  Slide the threaded rod through the top pillar holes and determine the required length allowing for the cap nuts.
Conduct required electrical tests.  Affix a  tested by  label.
Affix a batch number label.
Insert rear panel into the pillar.

Cut 2 x 80mm and 2 x 150mm strips of foam tape.
Affix to the inside of the lid.

 /
 
 

Place lid in position, run threaded rod through and fit requires washers and packing disks (See diagram) then secure.

  EMBED PBrush 
 
 
 
 
 

Affix a batch number label and Firtsflex contact detail label as show in photo.

Product code: SM16.10
Description: Temporary Power Distribution

 
 
ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS
 
Remove the lid then unscrew the top main terminal rail across the top.  This will allow better access to areas below.

 /
 
 
Make small marks level with the top of the switch window on the box.
Measure up 5mm from these and mark again (this is required as the socket plate is larger than the outlet).
Mark center points based on outlets above.

 /
 
 
Hold template socket plate in place based on markings and mark screw holes.
Drill these holes then attach the template back to front so it stands out from the box.
Use Dremel to router out the outlet openings.
 /
 
 
Cut the existing earth wire in a position that allows the junction to be secured to the socket plate once a lug is attached.
Terminate with a 4mm screw and washer to the socket plate to be installed.
 /
 
 
Unscrew the din rail behind RCD11.
Remove RCD from window.
Remove the blanking plates from the window so it is completely open.

 /
 
 

Cut all required wires based on wire cutting plan (see end of procedure).
Join the G/Y earth wires with a Corter T
Affix Corters to the rest of the wire ends.
Attach the RCDs to the DIN rail on the wire loom template board.
Follow the diagram on the wire loom template board to route the wires and locate in their corresponding positions and RCD connections.
Use cable ties at the stud positions.

 /
 
 

Remove the wire loom & RCDs ready to assemble in box.
Feed the RCDs into position near the existing RCD #11.
Attach all 3 RCDs to the DIN rail, feed through the window and secure to the rail brackets.

 /
 
 

Attach the 2 outlets, note there is ample room to connect the wires from the inside.
Feed the wires from the bottom of the RCDs to the outlets and attach. 

 /
 
 

On the top terminal rail release the end stop and make a space for an extra terminal between the black neutral and blue live terminal blocks.
Insert the extra terminal, push all terminals up tight against each other and secure the end stop.

 /
 
 

Remove the bridge between the existing neutral terminals and replace with one that will bridge the now three terminals.
Feed the wire loom from the top of the new RCDs to the top terminal rail.
Attach the wires to the appropriate positions, with the neutral going to the new terminal.
Connect the earth from the loom (from the outlets) to the available earth terminal space at the other end of this rail.
Reattach the top terminal rail.

 /
 
 

Insert caps over the outlet securing screws.
Mark the outlets and RCDs with ID and RCD Protected label.
 /
 /
 
 

Conduct QC electrical test.

Annual Testing for the METREL tester Procedure

NOTE: You can now carry out this test using the Autosequence test on the METREL tester called  Metrel Calibration Test :
/ Autosequence results will be saved at the end of the test.

NOTE: THE LAST STEP #18 ON THIS DOCUMENT IS MANDATORY

Scope: Verifying that the METREL tester is still within calibration

Requirements:
METREL Tester
METREL CALIBRATOR box 
Green test lead

/

Details:
The test is made up in 3 sections. Follow the instructions below closely and avoid any distractions.
Results must be recorded in a register on completion with a pass or fail.
If at any stage the test fails to meet the required values, report this to the Electrical Production Manager immediately. 
Testing is complete if results match expected results.

METREL Testing Procedure
Resistance Testing
Check the lead and box for any obvious damage
/

Plug in the 3 pin plug from the METREL CALIBRATOR into the METREL tester/

Plug one end of the green banana plug into the METREL tester BLACK socket labeled  P/S /
Plug the other end of the green banana plug into the GREEN 0.0&! socket/
Zero out the Metrel. Go to  Single tests 
/
Go to  CONT 
/

Press / to zero the Metrel with the test box. Resistance should read as R  _ _ _&!/

NOW PLEASE RUN THE AUTOSEQUENCE  CALIBRATION TEST  as it will log the following tests to record.

These steps below are only an example to what the Autosequence test will ask you to do; 

Touch inside the blue box to open up the  Parameters & Limits  menu/
Set the parameters as below. P/S   PE, 10A, 2S, 0.5&!
/
Plug the green cable into the 0.2&! socket on the box
/
Press the green button / to start the test. The result should show 0.20&! exactly after 2 seconds/
Plug the green cable into the 0.5&! socket on the box.
/
Press the green button / to test again. The result should show 0.50&! exactly after 2 seconds/
Isolation Testing   STEP 18 IS MANDATORY AFTER THR AUTOSEQUENCE TEST IS COMPLETE
Ensure the tester is plugged in as stated in step 2 under Resistance Testing.
From the main menu select  Single Tests 
 /
Select  ISO 
/
Touch inside the blue box to open the  Parameters & Limits  menu/
Set the parameters as below. Riso, 500V, 2s, Off. Return to the previous screen. /
Press the green button / to start the test. Press  YES  for the Warning! Prompt.
/
After 2 seconds the reading should show exactly 1.00 M&! with a voltage reading around 500V/
Confirm test voltage with a meter. Set a volt meter to the 1000V range and set it to DC.
Place one probe into the Neutral on the Metrel and the other into the LN socket on the METREL.
//

Press the green button / again to re-run the test. Your voltage on the volt meter should match the voltage on the Metrel +/- 10% 
/

The calibration verification is complete if all tests match the expected results. If results don t match expected parameters then notify the Production Manager ASAP.

Description: TUFFLITE 38W 5M IP65

/



 
 ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS
LIGHT BAR
Lay light assembly on bench.
Unhook the catches along the light cover and flip it back.
Unlock the supports from the LED panel and remove, check the micro switch is set to 4000K.
Remove the plastic bag containing the fixture plates and screws. This will be attached to the outer packing once completed.
Remove the gland from the end of the main compartment.
At the other end of the compartment, drill a hole sufficient to fit a 20mm gland using the moulded circle as a guide.
Fit both ends with 20mm glands.
 
 
 
CABLE
Determine which end of cable will be the connector end.
Measure 1450mm from this end, cut the cable and mark each side of the cut approx. 100mm back from edge to identify these as being the ends which will be inside the light compartment.
Strip back the inner and outer sheaths of all four ends using the rotary stripping machine (programs 9 and 10).
 
 
 
TERMINAL CONNECTING WIRES
Cut 300mm of red, black and green/yellow.
Strip both ends of each.
Affix corters to ONLY ONE end of each.
Insert the bare end of each into the MIDDLE terminal of the Wagos.
 
 
 
LIGHT ASSEMBLY
Feed the marked end of the SHORTER of the two sections of cable through the gland and pull through till it passes the second lock support for the LED panel.
Temporarily tighten the gland.
Feed the marked end of the LONGER of the two sections of cable through the other gland and pull through till it meets the other section.
Tighten the gland. 
 
 
 
THE INTENDED CONNECTOR / PLUG ENDS& 
Un-bind the braiding of the earth wires then twist together.
Affix a corter the heat shrink.
Strip back the insulation on the live and neutral wires and affix corters.
Connect the connector and plug.
Release the gland on the connector end and adjust the exposed cable so there is 300mm from the end of the connector to the gland.
Tighten the gland.
 
 
 
THE ENDS INSIDE LIGHT COMPARTMENT& 
Note; No corters required.
Un-bind the braiding of the earth wires then twist together.
Trim the end of the wire then heat shrink while leaving approx. 10mm of wire exposed at the end. 
Strip back the insulation on the live and neutral wires.
 
 
 
Connect all the wires inside the light compartment to the corresponding Wago connectors.
 /
 
 
Connect the live, neutral and earth wires from the wagos to the terminal affixed to the LED panel.
 /
 
 
Replace the LED panel and lock the supports.
Close the light cover.
 
 
 
Affix a Sitemate label on the back of the light housing.
Test and tag.
  EMBED PBrush 
 
 

Pack back in original box by cutting openings in the ends to allow cable to protrude.

A GRA can only be generated against what is on the original invoice. If a customer returns goods relating to more than one invoice a separate GRA will need to be raised for each individual invoice.

Customer Services - work from home parameters
The purpose of working from home is to provide some flexibility to team members. Initially this will be trialed for 3 months and if successful, may continue as a long term option for team members. Firstflex reserves the right to revoke working from home privileges if they feel it is not a suitable option for the department, or if it s being abused.
Guidelines:
Work from home days must be booked at least 1 week in advance.
Anyone working from home is expected to be working as you would be when in the office.
All requests must be submitted via the team calendar in Outlook and approved by the Customer Services Team Leader.
Requests will only be approved if there are no previous absences scheduled for that day.
Unless otherwise agreed, your hours of work are 8am   5pm. Normal break times apply.
Examples of what s acceptable:
Needing to be at home to let a tradesperson in.
Have an appointment close to home during the day (you would still be required to take leave for the time you are absent).
Wanting to avoid a long commute home due to long weekend traffic.
Examples of what it s not for:
Looking after sick kids   you will be required to take sick leave.
Alternative childcare option during the school holidays   you will be required to take annual leave.
Working from home between appointments without submitting a leave request.

DAMAGED IN TRANSIT PROCESS

       If our customer has Advised they have received goods damaged in transit we need to,
Organize a replacement to be sent asap.

Process a GRA for the damaged goods and send this off to the relevant staff member at the branch. CC in Inwards team so they have a copy of the paperwork, Both GRA and Invoice please.

Contact the carrier to advise them goods have been damaged. Best contact/s for our carriers are.
NZC: HYPERLINK "mailto:taylor.young@nzcouriers.co.nz"���� 
MAINFREIGHT: HYPERLINK "mailto:Connor.Hull@mainfreight.com" 
 OWENS: HYPERLINK "mailto:Sione.Ufi@owens.co.nz" 
Also, CC in their Customer service teams respectively.

Advise carrier that the Consignment has damage, and we would like it returned to us at there cost. It is always a good idea to get as much information as we can before contacting the carrier. i.e., was it signed for damaged, can we get photos of damaged goods. Can we get camera footage. This information can then be forwarded on in correspondence to the carrier.

Let the carrier know what the replacement Consignment is, and we would like it delivered at their cost. This is to be requested only if we deem the damage is though no fault of our own. i.e., poor packaging, cable to heavy for the drum etc. use your judgement 12

Keep a record of damaged consignments in your emails so we can back track if any issues come up.

What is a Financial Report?
Financial Report Writer (FRW) lets you generate reports that read data directly from your PRONTO-Xi General Ledger.
The reports are designed by combining:
A heading that defines the report title, default layout and output format
A set of rows, defining the General Ledger accounts from which to extract data
A set of columns, defining the financial data to display for the accounts in each row
The intersection of one row with one column is called a cell. Rows and columns can have the following various functions:
Some rows and columns will extract data only
Some rows and columns perform calculations using data from other columns and rows
Some rows and columns are for formatting only
A list of rows and columns types is included in this manual.
Why Create a Financial Report?
The Financial Report Writer (FRW) is a tool that lets you design layouts for financial reporting explicitly by extracting information data from the general ledger.
The FRW is designed to: 
Create Balance sheet and profit and loss reports
Total, consolidate, sort or select accounts based on sub-parts of the General Ledger account code
Total irregular groupings of accounts
Automate the substitution of a parameter (such as a cost centre or division code) in a report or automate the production of sets of related reports.
FRW will only read data from the General ledger tables.

Our current FX policy for pre-purchasing USD and EUR is not a true hedging procedure.��� 
Foreign currency purchase commitments from the various suppliers are pooled together (as opposed to contracts purchased per supplier/PO commitment) sorted and totalled by month of expected payment date, and a set % of that monthly total is purchased in relation to payment due dates.
/
The above has an averaging effect on our FX currency rate.�� This, together with the duration of the product cycle from date of purchase through to receipting into our warehouse makes it difficult to determine the correct rate and margin for a particular shipment/stock item.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
Change the current FX policy 

Purchase FX currency according to the individual PO amounts on the date that the PO is confirmed by the supplier and expected payment date/month as per the individual supplier terms of supply.

Decide on an appropriate minimum amount on whether to hedge or leave until spot rate  on payment date.  Eg. $ > 10,000   ??

Decide on a policy around the desired methodology/level of risk behind FX purchases, eg. Place an order on the board overnight or for longer period in anticipation of a preferable rate?  OR  accept the spot rate and purchase outright. 

  System rate vs daily spot rate. 
Our financial software is not cloud based so does not have the ability to interface with live spot currency rates.�� Instead the current practice is that an average FX rate is calculated at the beginning of each month and updated in the system.��� The calculation is �:
being the average FX rate of FX contracts purchased ( hedged )� +� 
(ii) the  unhedged  portion of purchase commitments at spot rate on the day that this calculation is completed� 
= �(iii) �Weighted average FX rate� +    buffer  of 3%� - to allow for exchange rate fluctuations during the month
This system rate is also used by our sales team when completing quotes to customers   hence the buffer element so we are not at risk of giving away margin.
This system rate forms the basis for calculating the realised FX gain/loss once payment is made to the supplier. 
Given this system rate is a constantly moving target, should the frequency of calculating this system rate be increased from just once a month?� any other alternative methods?
RECOMMENDATIONS:
Update the FX system rate on a more frequent basis, ideally daily. 

Calculation of the system rate to be based on the market spot rate on the day + a % buffer

Investigate the reasoning behind the current 3% buffer factor,  should this be more ?,  Paul to analyse actuals eg.  Difference between rate used on the day of quoting vs. the rate on the day of actual sale

  Mark to market valuations/ Unrealised FX gain/loss.
Currently we were only revaluing our mark-to-market contracts on a quarterly basis and not monthly.�� This causes timing issues as it is not correctly matching against the offset transactions of the realised FX gain/losses in the appropriate period - the amount of FX contracts held at any month end can be significant.
From July onwards it is intended to reflect Unrealised FX gain/losses on a monthly basis.
RECOMMENDATIONS:
Yes, reflect the mark to market valuation FX loss or gain on the hedged balances held at the end of a month on a monthly basis rather than quarterly

�Financial reporting:�� 
Currently we report the effect of all FX transactions (Realised and Unrealised) in our COGS section of the P&L.�� This can impact significantly on our gross margin and not entirely appropriate for management/Board interpretation and measurement against historical gross margins.
Should these FX gains/losses be reported in a separate section ?�� or Realised be included in COGS, but not Unrealised ??
RECOMMENDATIONS:
Yes, it is appropriate to reflect the Realised FX loss or gain in the COGS section of the P&L.  Unrealised FX loss or gain (ie. mark to market valuation)  are to be reported in a separate section eg. Other Income/Other Expenses

Summary of changes and outcomes
Incl confirming we will still have FX variations, however we will have a degree of greater certainty

Any anticipated risks / problems to consider?

RECOMMENDATIONS:
Yes, reflect the mark to market valuation FX loss or gain on the hedged balances held at any given month end on a monthly basis rather than quarterly

�Financial reporting:�� 
Currently we report the effect of all FX transactions (Realised and Unrealised) in our COGS section of the P&L.�� This can impact significantly on our gross margin and not entirely appropriate for management/Board interpretation and measurement against historical gross margins.
Should these FX gains/losses be reported in a separate section?�� or Realised be included in COGS, but not Unrealised ??

RECOMMENDATIONS:
Yes, it is appropriate to reflect the Realised FX loss or gain in the COGS section of the P&L.  Unrealised FX loss or gain (ie. mark to market valuation)  are to be reported in a separate section eg. Other Income/Other Expenses

Major Function Flag
 Description
 
 General Ledger Posting Splits
 
 By Territory
 Posts the sales and cost of sales to the General Ledger using the SN (Sales   Normal Item) and CN (Cost of Goods Sold   Normal Item) special accounts respectively. These special accounts can be split by territory of the customer.
Specify the number of characters to be used from the customer s territory code when constructing the special account name.
For example, if this flag is set to  2 , the special accounts SNtt and CNtt are used when posting sales and cost of sales where  tt  is the first two characters of the customer s territory code from the sales order.
Sales of special items are posted to the General Ledger using the SS (Sales   Special Item) and CS (Cost of Goods Sold   Special Item) special accounts. These are split by customer s territory according to the setting of this flag.
A value of zero indicates that special accounts are not to be split by territory.
 
 By Item Group
 This flag is similar to the  By Territory  flag where it defines the number of characters from the code to use when constructing the special account name.
 
 By Group/Branch
 This flag is used to overlay/mask the branch or territory over the selected G/L account code as selected from the special accounts file, at a particular character. It is used for special account connected to Sales Orders (SN), Rental (RN) and Project Costing (JC) modules, based on the branch code.
For example, if the G/L account returned for Sales - Group  ABCD  (special account SNABCD) is 190000000 and we wish to post to branch  99  for this group, with this flag set to  6 , we mask the branch over the G/L account code, returning the result of 190009900. This code is then validated in the normal manner.
Specify the character position in the General Ledger account code from where to overlay the branch code. 
 
 
 0
 No masking.
 
 
 1-9
 Overlay branch on G/L account starting at this character position
 
 
 A-D
 Overlay branch starting at position 10 through 13 respectively.
Setting this flag to  C  (12) and overlaying a 4 digit branch (for example,  1234 ) would result in an invalid G/L account code as the last digit of the branch  4  would be truncated due to the size limitation of the G/L account code.
 
 
 G
 G/L mask stored in  job-out-reference  field on the project cost master.
 
 
 P
 Overlay G/L account code using Project Costing PMCs (Positional Mapping Codes). For full details, refer to the System Administration reference manual.
 
 Inventory By Group
 Records the value of inventory in the General Ledger by posting to the special account IN (Warehouse Inventory) whenever a stock movement/re valuation affects the value of stock-on-hand. This account can be split by warehouse code. Depending on the value of this flag, this special account can also be split by item group. This makes it possible to maintain special accounts in the Balance Sheet recording the value of stock-on-hand by item group within the warehouse.
Specify the number of characters to be used from the item group code of the item when constructing the special account name.
For example, if this flag is set to  2 , the special account INwwwwppp is used when posting inventory accounts, where  wwww  is the code of the warehouse where the stock movement occurred, and  pp  is the first two characters of the item group code.
This special account must have a warehouse code of four characters. If the warehouse codes are less than four characters, spaces must be inserted in the special account name before the item group code. For example  INMLB PP  where there should be a space before  PP .
To not split inventory postings by item group, enter the value  0 .

SV   Stocktake Variance;
IV   Inventory Purchase Cost Variance;
IR   Inventory Revaluation;
SC   Manufactured Items Scrapped;
QA   Quality Assurance Rejects.
For further information on these special account codes refer, to the System Administration reference manual.
 
 Customers Control
 The DCTRL special account (Accounts Receivable Control) special account can be split according to the territory of the customer.
Specify the number of characters to be used from the customer s territory code when constructing a special account name.

NEW SUPPLIER ACCOUNT OPENING PROCESS
In most cases, opening a new supplier account will start when you receive an account application form from a Firstflex staff member (they have found a new supplier for something they want to purchase or service they want to have done).
To fill out the account application, use the  Company details  pdf page saved in Q:/AAGeneral/Office Admin.
For references, scan through the list of suppliers in Accounts Payable in Pronto to find ones that are used regularly and for a substantial $$ amount each month.  Using a variation of suppliers is good so that you re not bugging the same ones all the time.  Some examples of suppliers to use as references are; Cimplas, Snells Packaging, Profile Extrusions, Polyprint Packaging, Dometic, Velocity, Aluminium Extrusion Co etc.  Find their phone numbers from their AP supplier details page.
Scan and send the application back to the supplier and set them up in Pronto
Go to Accounts Payable/Maintain Supplier/Maintain Supplier Accounts/ 

/

To add a new supplier, enter E
Fill in the standard information for the supplier, Name, Address, Phone, payment terms, bank account number etc.
Payment type   Enter a D for foreign suppliers only as these are paid separately from all other suppliers.
All other (local) suppliers should have an E entered in Payment type and you will be taken to the bank account number screen, after entering the Bank and Branch codes you happen to get a pop up saying that the branch code doesn t exist, you will need to add the code (two digits, 4 digits) to the table by selecting MAINTAIN in the table and then E to add a new one.
If it is a Stock supplier, Enter STK once you get to the  Supplier Group  field, this will add it to the correct Yellowfin reports we need it to appear in.
Air, Sea, Local Cover fields are entered by the purchasing department so enter over/leave blank.
Foreign suppliers require the Tax Code: E and Tax Exemption code: Y when you get to these fields   this is so that the GST is calculated as nil when the purchasing team raise purchase orders/shipments on these suppliers.
From time to time, staff will request an account to be set up for a supplier that has not needed an account application to be filled out.
If the new supplier is a NON-STOCK supplier, ask the staff member to fill out form 510 from Master Copies Forms in Q Drive.
If the new suppler is a STOCK supplier   which will usually be requested by someone in purchasing   you can set them up in Pronto straight away as the transactions on these suppliers are generated via purchase orders and shipments, and by people outside of the admin department where Audit information is system generated and therefore meeting internal control requirements.
In either case, ask them to also provide a copy of a quote or invoice   something that will provide all the information needed to complete the set up in Pronto.

detail:
ORDER ENTRY PROCEDURE
Programs that you will need to have open before you start
Dispatch  ( NZC ticketing program) 
User name: super
Password: money
Mainchain / freeman web 
User name: aflexcables
Password: password1
Cable weights spreadsheet
Under Q drive, warehouse folder
Pronto 2 x sessions	
Before you start to process an order, check the following
What lengths does the customer need (e.g 100 s, 50 s etc)
Are we charging the customer freight (freight is charged when the order is under $250.00)
Is the order going via courier or truck (work out weights and cubes using the cable weights spreadsheet)   if you don t know how to work out what it will be sent on make a note on the packing slip and the warehouse staff will get back to you
Stamp the order with order entry stamp 

Stamp with Sales stamp and pass over to sales team if& 
We do not have enough stock
You need lengths verified
If you think the order needs to go by truck ( order will not be received overnight if going to the south island ) 
If you need to know the colour the cable they are after
Be sure to write down on the stamp why you have passed it to sales

You are now ready to click into pronto
Once you have one session open to open a second one click on the  new Session  icon in the grey panel at the top of the page 
Now click on your company   Firstflex Cables  
Click on Sales orders and then full order entry
Check the date is correct and press enter
Enter the customer code 
Enter down to customer Ref ( customer purchase order # )
Check the address that pops up                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   is correct & enter down to price on Del Doc. Enter N
At this point you can make changes to the delivery address or customer ref, select C to correct customer ref or select A to change the delivery address 
Once you are happy with these details select L for line to start your order
Enter your products code and quantity on order and check price matches if it doesn t stamp the order with the sales stamp and pass it over to the sales team to look into
At the start of the order you may need to add a note line for a quote ref
If everything is correct once you get to the end of the line. The available lots will pop up from here and you can select what lot # the warehouse staff will cut the cable from- please only use 100s or 50 mtr lengths for 100 or 50 mtr orders.
Once you have entered all products on the order you will then enter your freight line by selecting a new line and pressing the C key your freight options will come up 
0 = customer collect
1 = freight free
2 = North island freight $9.50
3 = South island freight $14.40
4 = Special charge you can enter your own amount i.e SSR, SATURDAY DELIVERY 
You may also need to add a note line under your freight line for things like your truck name and con note #, Saturday delivery, GBS ETC
Fill in the order entry stamp on the original customer s order 
To print your order now press esc twice and select P for print. This will print your packing slip but you will also need a Delivery Docket. 
In the left column below Full order entry click on Despatch. Here you will type in your packing slip number and then click complete OK which will print your Delivery docket
In your second Pronto session you will have you curve labels screen, using the following steps as you did to get to Sales orders click on User sales order programs and select curve labels
In your curve labels screen you then re type your packing slip number and press F11 to print your labels

NZ Couriers 
Go into the dispatch IT screen
Click on new shipment ( highlighted in blue at the bottom of the screen ) 
Enter your packing slip number and the address should pop up the same as what is on your packing slip.
Enter the number or drums/boxes/satchels in the correct line
Print (F12)

Owens/ Mainfreight
Go into the Freeman web and select either Owens or Mainfreight (the process is the same for both)
Select new consignment & enter customers code this should be the same as Pronto
Enter customer order number in the receiver ref
Enter your initials and XX in the senders ref i.e AIXX
Enter what you are sending (1 x carton 0.046 25kg)
In note number you will enter either AFL or AFO and the packing slip number this will be the tracking number and click on quote this will bring up the cost.
Where you had entered your initials and XX ad the cost after to the nearest round figure (AIXX40)
When you have checked all the details are correct, press print to print a manifest and packing label

GBS
You can print your GBS address label from the same program you print your curve labels by pressing F10 you will need one address label per item you are sending so 5 items you will need to print 5 labels
The GBS forms are in a green folder on the desk you will need only one of these per order 

Orders with prints
When you receive an order that the customer wants the cable printed you will need to put this on the packing slip. 
To do this on a new line at the beginning of the order enter the code  print  this will bring up your print options ( print with charge, print without charge)
Select what print you are after then enter the quantity of cable you want printed anything 100 mtrs and over will be free.
Enter a note line under this and type out the print the customer wants (STOLEN FROM & .)
Complete order as normal and pass all paper work to Frank for the print to be signed off to avoid errors

Saturday delivery
When you receive an order that needs to be a Saturday delivery you process just like you would a normal order.
After you have entered your freight line add a note line saying **SATURDAY DELIVER** under this line add another note line with *SAT DEL   and the number of your Saturday delivery ticket (found in the top draw on your right.
Print as normal

RETURNED GOODS POLICY

CONDITIONS FOR RETURNING GOODS
All products returned must be in good order and condition; acceptance is subject to inspection.
Firstfex Cables will accept for return without reservation the following:
� Any product supplied incorrectly
� Any product not to its given standard due to design error, faulty manufacture, damage in transit or where Firstflex Cables is at fault or otherwise responsible.
No goods will be accepted for return without prior consultation and acceptance (see GRA process below).
All claims to be made within 30 days of original dispatch or as otherwise agreed in writing.
Firstflex Cables reserves the right to apply a restocking fee for goods returned based on the value of the goods returned plus G.S.T. and/or freight costs.
Products/Lengths that will not be accepted for return are:
� Specific manufactured to order or purchased to order (specially procured or indented) product;
� Lengths cut to customer s order   less than minimum as determined by the Sales Manager.

PROCEDURE FOR RETURNING GOODS
For all returns, a GRA (Goods Return Authorisation) must be obtained from a member of the customer services team at Firstflex Cables. Please phone 09 2641000 or email HYPERLINK "mailto:sales@firstflex.co.nz" for this.
Firstflex Cables shall return the GRA to you within two working days, by email.
This shall indicate:
� Acceptance when issued with a GRA number and duly signed by the Sales Manager.
� Refusal when marked DECLINED through the body of the form and duly signed by the Sales Manager.
A copy of the authorized GRA must accompany the goods being returned. Any goods arriving without proper documentation may be turned away at the originator s expense.
Freight costs incurred are the responsibility of the originator   unless Firstflex Cables is responsible for the reason for the return.
The GRA is an authorisation for return and not an agreement to credit. All returns are subject to inspection.
All credits will be to a specific account; ie, no cash reimbursements.

About this So Easy Education Guide
This education guide in the  So Easy Education  series provides a comprehensive overview of the sales order creation and maintenance process using the PRONTO-Xi Sales Orders module.
Some screens/instructions and so on in this guide may differ from your system depending on the major function flag settings that you have set in your PRONTO-Xi Sales Orders implementation.
Course Description
The PRONTO-Xi Sales Orders Processing Education Guide provides a comprehensive course on all of the aspects of sales order processing in PRONTO-Xi.
This course will provide information on the following:
An understanding of how to enter and maintain different types of sales orders.
How to process backorders
How to cancel orders
Setting up alternative items for use in orders
Transferring sales orders
Returning stock into the warehouse
Processing kit orders
And also reporting on various aspects of sales orders.
Participants in this course will gain an understanding of PRONTO-Xi Sales Orders transactional capabilities and its relationship to other modules in PRONTO-Xi.
Prerequisites
In this guide, it is assumed that:
Attendees have completed training in PRONTO-Xi Navigation and Overview, and are familiar with the general functionality available in PRONTO-Xi.
Attendees have an understanding of the basic sales order lifecycle, the nature of inventory and customers.

After working through this guide, the attendees should be able to complete the steps necessary to process a sale, beginning with creating an order, through despatching, to producing the final invoice using PRONTO-Xi Sales Orders.
The sales order entry operator should also understand how to manage all aspects of a sales order, such as is described in this course.

About the Sales Orders module
PRONTO Xi Sales Orders is an order entry and invoicing system suitable for the needs of a wide variety of businesses. It handles the processing of sales orders, including production of picking slips, despatch of goods, and printing of consignment notes, delivery dockets, labels and invoices.
Numerous options and flag settings, aided further by the power of the Applistructure suite of tools, enable the user interface and order processes to be tailored to meet local requirements. Variations in the way normal orders are entered provide the ability to process a wide variety of order types including credit notes, forward orders, quotations, consignment orders, inter-warehouse transfers, direct ship orders - as well as to control Return Management Authorities.
PRONTO Xi Sales Orders is fully integrated with PRONTO Xi Inventory, Accounts Receivable and General Ledger, with further interfaces to other modules where a Sales Order process forms part of the transaction flow - including Service, Manufacturing and Project Costing. Inventory levels, customer balances and relevant General Ledger accounts are updated when a sales order is completed.

The feature set in sales order processing includes the following:
User-defined order entry screen
Picking slips, consignment notes, delivery dockets, labels, invoices
Backorders released by priority, percentage filled or dollar value
Transfer/work orders for unavailable stock
Credit and recharge by invoice or line item
Integrated with telemarketing
Up to date recording of available stock at time of order entry/edit

Email the Credit Release Officer if customer exceeds credit limit
Duplicate customer reference (customer order number) checking
Multiple warehouse capabilities
Direct links between sales orders, purchase orders and work orders
Foreign currency

Warning notes for display at order entry time
Scheduling / splitting / copying or merging of orders
Customised forms (invoices, picking slips delivery dockets etc.)
Various search facilities for finding an order
Last price history can be called up in sales order lines
Selection of delivery addresses if more than one for the customer
Powerful audit reporting
Discounting options
Kit processing, recording of serial numbers and lot numbers
Discontinued / obsolete stock
Cost adjustment orders
Full history recording
Powerful sales management tools including enquiries; standard reports; user-defined reports
Stock alternatives and multiple selling units
Full backorder tracking.

Timing of Presentation of Financial Reports
The board have moved that all of the source data should be delivered to Campbell Tyson within 10 working days of the end of the financial period.  Campbell Tyson should complete the financial statements and have them transmitted to the board members within 15 days of the end of the financial period and the board meeting should be no earlier than 20 working days after the end of the period.
Quarter End period information should be supplied in April (for March), July (for June), October (for September) and January (for December).
Documents and Reconciliations to be provided by Firstflex to Campbell Tyson are below.

 GST Returns processed during the quarter.  A one month GST reconciliation needs to be provided if the GST period doesn t align with the quarter end month. Eg for June quarter, GST for the month of June will need to be reconciled on its own as the prior GST Return was for the April   May period, the next one June   July period.  Follow the GST Return procedure   document 502.
 
 
 4.
 Copies of all invoices supporting asset purchases during the quarter.  Davinder/Campbell Tyson will provide the depreciation adjustment to make with the aligning journals once the final accounts have been prepared.  No need for us to process a Depreciation amount until then.
 
 
 5.
 Copies of Donation receipts, provide these once per year for the whole year in April,

 8.
 A list of staff loans (if any) that reconcile to GL account 19912.
 
 
 9.
 Accounts Payable ATB.  This was also printed as part of month end process.

General Policy Objectives
The overall financial objective of this policy is to protect the Sales Margin of Firstflex Cables.

Delegated Authorities, Segregation of Duties
The Administration team is authorized to transact existing FX Contracts;
Orders/purchases of new Foreign Currency contracts can only be done by a Director and confirmations signed off by a Director.

Foreign Exchange Management
FX Requirements and reporting is to be managed by the Administration team and the  FX Contracts vs Purchases  file is to be updated and given to the Directors & GM fortnightly.

Approved Dealing Counterparties & Limits
Foreign Currency contracts can only be purchased from ANZ National Bank or as advised by a Director or GM.

Approved Hedging Instruments
The Types of Instruments used by Firstflex Cables are primarily Forward Contracts and some option structures as advised by a Director or GM.  Knock out options and option structures without a worse case rate fall outside the limits of the policy and are not to be used.

Minimum & Maximum Hedging Limits
As the company nears the expected date of the cash flows, the level of certainty and the rates likely to be faced increases.  Therefore the percentage of cover taken will increase as we get closer to the date of expected cash flows.

KPIs entered and Saved in Q:\Caths Folder\HOD & Board\HOD Info\Monthly KPIs

To be done and copied into Meetings/HOD Meetings Folder by the first Friday following each month end.
These two KPIs are entered on the  FX  sheet of the workbook.

DAYS DEBTORS;
Find the Net Sales figure of the month report is for.  Needs to be after the Rebate provision accounts have been reconciled and adjusted as part of month end process.  This is found on the  PLBA  Profit and Loss Actual/Budget comparison report out of GL reporting in Pronto.  (Example reports are attached).
Divide that figure by the number of days in the month.  This is the Sales per Day figure.
Now from the Debtors ATB report (jasper), take the total Debtors balance and deduct GST.  (Example calculations follow this instruction page).
Divide the GST excl. debtors total by the daily sales figure.  This is the overall Days Debtors KPI.
Corys and Ideal have special terms where they can pay on the 1st of the month 2 months following invoice date.  We do another calculation taking this into account to reflect a more accurate KPI, to calculate this, take the total debtors figure from the ATB again (GST incl.)
Deduct Cory s and Ideal s payments made on the 1st of the month.
Deduct the GST from this figure and divide that again by the daily sales figure.  This is the Days Debtors KPI, taking into account Corys and Ideal special terms.
Both KPIs are reported for comparison month by month.  Our usual range is between 40   45 days overall and 30   35 days after Corys and Ideal payments are taken into account.  A figure outside these ranges will mean we had customers pay late and is not good for cashflow.

FX/PURCHASING;
The forward FX Cover section of the page is really a duplicate of the information in the FX Contracts spreadsheet maintained as part of the AP International supplier purchases function.
Take the monthly requirements and monthly purchased totals and enter them in the appropriate currency section (i.e. USD, AUD, and EUR).  Copy across the average currencies also.  Now update the graph so that it picks up the current/newly entered figures.  Look up the system rates in Pronto   under Administration tab/System Admin/System codes & messages/Local-Foreign currency maintenance/Currency maintenance/Local-Foreign Currency Maintenance.
For the Purchases Graph; skip to the  FX Purchases  sheet in the KPIs workbook   should be next to the FX sheet you are working in.
From the Yellowfin Report    Stock Supplier Orders in NZ$.......  (copy attached), take the totals for each month and copy these into the FX Purchases spreadsheet in the matching month.
Enter the FX gain from GL account 12250 in the matching month and then update the graph to include your new figures.

Creating the Commercial Invoice 
Ensure you have weight and dimensions of the item you are sending before starting.
Q: Drive \ AA General Info \ Commercial Invoices & Proforma Invoice
Select the supplier you are sending goods to
Click on date modified to put all the invoices in date created order.
Click into the most recent commercial invoice to open it.
Click File.
Click Save As.
Click Browse - it should come up where all the other invoices for that supplier are saved.
Save as a new invoice and change the date at the end to today s date.

Update the following fields:
Date of Export:			enter today s date.
International Waybill No:	enter the Toll Air Waybill Number
Full Description of Goods:	specifically what you are sending.
Quantity: 			the quantity being sent
Unit: 				the unit measure e.g. metre, each etc. 
Unit Value:			the buy price for that item.
Total Weight:			the total weight of all goods being sent.
Dimensions:			the total cubic metres or dimensions of all goods being sent.
Date:				enter today s date (bottom right corner).
Save
Print 3 x copies on Firstflex letterhead
Get the sender of the goods to sign each of the 3 original copies.
Photocopy 1 of the originals for our ref.

Completing the Toll Airway Bill   see example below
Box 1:	Check the AWB# matches that on the commercial invoice you created.
Box 2:	Tick Charge Sender.
Box 4:	Sign write today s date.
Box 5:	Write the company name, address, city, country, postcode and phone number.
Box 7:	Tick Permanent Export and Charge Sender.
Box 8:	Service Type = Economy Door to Door.
	Description of Contents = description of goods being sent e.g.  Electrical Goods (Samples) 
	Size & Weight = write the total quantity, weight and dimensions
Photocopy the completed Airway Bill for our reference.

Packing and distributing the goods 
Put a lock re-sealable bag on the box. If you are using a satchel, there is already one provided.
Put the original AWB and the 3 original commercial invoices in the lock re-sealable bag on the box or satchel.
If on the box, tape down all sides of the lock re-sealable bag.
Write in vivid clearly on the box or satchel the WB# and the ultimate destination.
Ring Toll on 0800 231531 and book a collection.
Write down the booking ref and track until goods have arrived at the destination.

If the caller asks for a staff member by name, say:  I will check if ____is available, who can I say is calling? 
If the caller asks for a staff member by name but that person is busy/unavailable/out of the office, TELL the caller what time/day that particular person is due back.  Then:

Transferring Calls 
When talking to a customer, press the  Transfer  key
Dial the extension to transfer to, then select the type of transfer   BlindTrnf or AttTrnf 
BlindTrnf: The call is transferred immediately, so just hang up. 
AttTrnf: This gives you a chance to speak to the person you are transferring to.  Once you have announced the caller, just hang up.
If the person you are transferring to doesn t want the call he / she can hang up and the call comes back to you.

Putting Calls on Hold 
Press the Hold (pause) button at the lower right side of the phone.

To take the caller off hold, press resume button on screen

A GRA can only be generated against what is on the original invoice. If a customer returns goods relating to more than one invoice a separate GRA will need to be raised for each individual invoice.

The process is split into 3 steps to be performed by the following people: 
Creating a GRA   Customer Services
Processing Authorised Returns into the Warehouse   Accounts Administrator (with the possibility of Returns and Inwards Goods Coordinator taking over)
Converting a GRA into a Credit Note   Accounts Administrator

The customers original invoice number
A Credit Request from the customer

Print the invoice

Enter the customer code.
In the Type field, enter R.

Enter (a new note line will automatically come up)
