EMPLOYEE TRAVEL ON COMPANY BUSINESS
All company related expenses must be clearly justified for business related purposes and the employee s choice of travel provider should take into account: cost, efficiency of route and use of preferred supplier
All travel must have the prior approval of the Managing Director.
Employees are free to join personal frequent flyer programmes, however, any costs associated with joining such programmes must be met by the employee.
Employees are to fly economy class for all domestic and international travel. In some circumstances business class travel may be approved by the Managing Director.
Where possible, no more than two senior managers of the company should travel on the same flight.
The company will reimburse reasonable expenses incurred during company travel provided sufficient supporting documentation is provided. Accommodation and food costs should be restricted to mid-range establishments.
Travel insurance is provided for employees on authorised company business outside their usual country of residence.
Questions in respect of employee travel should be directed to the Managing Director.
Expenses:
All items purchased on a company credit card will require an itemised invoice/receipt and approval.
All receipts must be sent to admin via the  smart receipts  app. 
All expenses must be approved by an appropriate departmental manager and forwarded to accounts with relevant documentation and receipts attached.
Reimbursement will be via direct credit, upon submission of a Pay Reimbursement Form, with relevant approval.
Employees are entitled to claim for relevant business related calls made from their home telephone or personal mobile phone supported by relevant documentation.
Questions in respect to expenses should be directed to the Managing Director.

Travel Guidelines
Overnight travel requires a  Travel Request Form  to be completed at least 6 weeks in advance of planned trips (Q: Drive \ Master Copies Forms \ Reps Forms \ 277 Travel Request Form).
Corporate Traveller will book the airport parking but they need to know which car park to book (usually Carpark M or Carpark O).
As the car parks are always changing you need to check carparks from time to time at HYPERLINK "https://www.aucklandairport.co.nz/airport-parking/book-a-car-park". The average car park cost should be around $70- $80, any more please see the Marketing Assistant or Sales Manager.
The Sales Manager must authorise any changes to the original booking before changing the booking. Contact Corporate Traveller to make changes.
All expense receipts must be submitted to the Sales Manager on your return.
If you want to extend your trip for personal reasons, you must obtain permission from the Sales Manager before booking. 
Any personal expenses charged to the company will be deducted from your next pay.

Important Notes:
Lower fluid levels may reduce the battery capacity and reduce the service life of the battery.
Higher liquid levels may lead to electrolyte overflow when charging, which may cause corrosion to the battery compartment or the vehicle.
The hoists should be put on charge every Fridays at the end of the day so they are ready to be topped up on Monday morning.
Do not tip the liquid content from the bucket onto the concrete as it will leave a permanent acid stain.

PPE gear, gloves and glasses must be worn at all times when using the battery water refill equipment.

Before you begin check the condition of the cable leads, cells and especially dry acid build-up.
Report any issues to the Warehouse Manager.

If the red buoy is not floating, top up the cells with distilled water from the bucket.
Correct Water Level: The white line should just be showing. This is also visible through the transparent filler caps. 

Top up the battery cells using the jug and funnel or the hand pump.

If you over fill or find the cells are already over filled, you must remove the excess water.
Wrong Water Level: The white line on the buoy is fully showing.

Excess battery water must be sucked out with the hand pump and put back into the distilled water bucket.

Content: Cable InformationAll cable leaving the premises must have a brand / size / voltage embossed or printed on the cable unless on the exceptions list below: SIHF / SICY HCT / HCS / HCSF / HCTCY / HCSCY / HCTF / HCM / HCMHF / HCMHFX / HCK6HCY / HCP / HCG3 / HCE3 / HCG1 / HC3CV7CMS / MTS / MBS / MFE / MTRAll extra low voltage cables which are wound onto drums must not leave the premises without a â€œCaution not suitable for mains connection E.L.V. onlyâ€ sticker placed on the drum. Dan to check thisAll cable must be meter marked if over 30 metres in length, unless otherwise stated. All cables that are metre marked must have a start and finish length recorded on the curve label. Cables are to be printed in black only. How to wind and package cable:Find an appropriate drum to suit the type of cable to be wound off: Ensure the bending radius of the cable suits the bending radius on the drum. Put multi core, screened and SWA cables on drums with big bores to prevent breakage or on hand winder then wrap with plastic wrap. Cable Information
All cable leaving the premises must have a brand / size / voltage embossed or printed on the cable unless on the exceptions list below: 
SIHF / SICY 
HCT / HCS / HCSF / HCTCY / HCSCY / HCTF / HCM / HCMHF / HCMHFX / HCK6

MS / MTS / MBS / MFE / MTR
All extra low voltage cables which are wound onto drums must not leave the premises without a  Caution not suitable for mains connection E.L.V. only  sticker placed on the drum. Dan to check this
All cable must be meter marked if over 30 metres in length, unless otherwise stated. 
All cables that are metre marked must have a start and finish length recorded on the curve label. 
Cables are to be printed in black only.
 
How to wind and package cable:
Find an appropriate drum to suit the type of cable to be wound off: 
Ensure the bending radius of the cable suits the bending radius on the drum. 
Put multi core, screened and SWA cables on drums with big bores to prevent breakage or on hand winder then wrap with plastic wrap. Ignoring the bending radius on SWA cables will cause severe defects to the cable once it is pulled off the drum.
Once the drum is mounted onto the cable winder, pull the cable through the metre mark counter and secure it tightly to the drum.  
Wind the cable on to the drum.
If cable is being printed be careful on speed so as not to distort printing.
Cable rolls must not exceed the outer flange diameter of the cable reel.
Short lengths of small cable can be pulled manually through meter counter.
Use the hand winder for short lengths of larger cables and SWA.  
Cut off the desired amount, tie plastic wrap to end of the cable and wrap around 3 -4 times.
If cable is meter marked, always cut on the meter marks (as long as meter marks are correct and accurate).
If rolling 20m or less of cable, shrink wrap the cable, then tape or cable tie the ends. 
If the hand roll is small, pack it into a suitably sized box. 

How to pick accessories and non-lot tracked cable:
Go to the allocated bin location displayed on the PICKING SLIP and pick corresponding components with order.  
Use separate plastic bags for each different product and label each bag. 

Conduit 
Lengths must be in manageable weight bundles, securely taped together with address secured onto bundle with plastic wrap. 
All conduit lengths are sent via Mainfreight, Transauck and Owens (unless collected).  
Packing slip to be stuck and taped on with clear tape. 

Galvanised Fittings
Pack smaller conduit fittings into separate plastic bags for every different product, packed well (not loose) and boxed.  
The Distribution Manager (or 2IC) will advise whether boxed conduit fittings or other boxed accessories should be attached to the conduit or not for truck freight. 
All galvanised fittings and accessories must always be rust free when dispatched.
To clean fittings before dispatch, use the wire brush nozzles to remove any rust (nozzles are located on the work bench).
Flexible Conduit (metal or PVC)
Place flexible conduit on metre marked floor or pull it carefully through the meter counter and cut to ordered length.
Cut by grabbing with both hands and snapping, then snip the conduit between the 2 breaks.
If flexible conduit is PVC coated (GFCP) or GFCLT, you will need to neatly cut the PVC with a knife first.
Pack in the appropriate bag, box or on a reel.

Receiving goods:
Check for damage.  
If the goods are damaged, note the type of damage on the carriers consignment note e.g. broken drum, damaged cable etc.
Check the correct number of pallets and/or cartons have been delivered.
Sign for the goods after you have checked for damage and all parcels are accounted for.
If signing for goods but you are not in the Inwards Goods team, notify inwards of their arrival and location.

Once the carrier has departed: 
Check all goods are correct as per the  pre shipment list .  
Packing slips need to be verified by Warehouse Manager against  pre shipment list  and signed.

Sitemate Order: Refer to Sitemate Quality Control Procedure 400SM

Cable samples: confirm with the Operations Manager if samples are required. 
Place the samples in a small box or bag and label with vessel name or shipment code. 
Give the samples to the assembly team for a full general check.  
If a problem is found, quality control needs to be involved.
Once goods have been checked off against the packing slip, give all paperwork to the Purchasing Supervisor.
Small inwards goods orders: put directly into the inwards goods area.
Goods from large overseas orders: keep together until checked.

If a problem is found the Purchasing Manager (Rissie or Bruce??) needs to be involved.

Goods returned for credit: 
Check length and / or quantity of goods returned. 
Write what the customer has physically returned in the returns book.  
Remove the top copy and attach to the GRA paperwork.
Give the paperwork to the Administration team so the credit can be processed.
This should occur within 2 working days.
At the end of the month these need to be receipted in immediately and given to the paperwork given to the Admin team for processing.

Objective:  	To effectively screen new product opportunities to decide if they are worth 		introducing to the product mix.

Action Steps:	Ask the following screening questions about the product, to determine where it fits on a scale from 1 being definitely NO and 5 being definitely YES.

REAL - Is there a real market for this product? Questions below focus on the Market.

 
 Screening Questions
 Comments
 Scale 1 to 5
 
 Is there a need or desire for the product?

 
 
 
 Can the customer buy it direct?

 
 
 
 Is the size of the potential market adequate?

 
 
 
 Will the customer buy the product?

 
 
 
 Are there subjective barriers to purchasing it?

 
 
 
 Is there a clear concept?

 
 
 
 Can the product be made?

 
 
 
 Could it be created with available technology and materials, or would it require a breakthrough of some sort?
 
 
 
 If it can be created, can it be produced and delivered cost effectively or would it be so expensive that potential customers would shun it?
 
 
 
 Will the final product satisfy the market?

 
 
 
 

WIN   Can we gain and maintain a competitive edge? Questions below focus on being competitive

 
 Screening Questions
 Comments
 Scale 1 to 5
 
 Can the product be competitive?

 
 
 
 Are there any features and benefits?

 
 
 
 Does it have a competitive advantage?

 
 
 
 Can someone else s offering provide customers with the same results or benefits?

 
 
 
 Can the advantage be sustained?

 
 
 
 How will competitors respond?

 
 
 
 If we were going to attack our own product, what vulnerabilities would we find?  How can we reduce them?

 
 
 
 Would the product survive a sustained price war?

 
 
 
 Can our company be competitive?

 
 
 
 Do we have superior resources?

 
 
 
 Do we have appropriate management?

 
 
 
 Does the Company have direct or related experience with the market?

 
 
 
 Are the Company s development-process and skills appropriate for the scale and complexity of the project?
 
 
 
 Does the project both fit the company culture and have a suitable champion?

 
 
 
 Can we understand and respond to the market?

 
 
 
 
WORTH IT   Will the expected payoff be worth the risks involved? Questions below focus on risks vs. payoffs.
 
 Screening Questions
 Comments
 Scale 1 to 5
 
 Will the product be profitable at an acceptable risk?

 
 
 
 Are the forecasted returns greater than costs?

 
 
 
 Are risks acceptable?
Effort / Return Ratio

 
 
 
 How will small changes in price, market share, and launch timing affect cash flows and break-even points?
 
 
 
 Does launching the product make strategic sense?

 
 
 
 Does the product or service fit our overall growth strategy?

 
 
 
 Will it enhance the company s capabilities by for example, driving expansion of manufacturing, human capital, logistics, or other functions?
 
 
 
 Will it have a positive or negative impact on brand equity?

 
 
 
 Will it cannibalize or improve sales of the company s existing products?

 
 
 
 Will it enhance or harm relationships with stakeholders?

 
 
 
 Does the project create opportunities for follow-on business or new markets that would not be possible otherwise?
 
 
 
 Is the product suitable for its intended environment e.g. UV, chemicals etc. Has it been used by other distributors overseas, what was their feedback. 
 
 
 
 Will the product be perceived as low, mid, or high end? Is it an old copy, good mid-range  or new and innovative

Content: Contacts: Dan, Dean, NauIn the event of the loss of power, the automatic transfer switch will send a signal to the generator to start up and transfer the power back to the switch board. The Operation Manger will also be notified by Vector of the power outage This will supply power to all areas of our business including winders, top office and kitchen. The crisis team will determine what equipment can be used at the time of the power outage based on the outage, time of outage, weather and time of day.The downstairs and upstairs office aircon will automatically be isolated (turned off) when there is a power cut to reduce the load to the generator on start up. The aircon in the server room will remain running at all times. Once the generator is running you can activate the downstairs and upstairs office aircon - refer to page 2 for Aircon activationThe generator fuel level will be monitored monthly as part of the Firstflex maintenance plan. The fuel level will be kept at 60L 50% at all times. In the event of the loss of power after work hours the generator will continue to supply power to our business overnight until we arrive the next morningIn the event that the generator does not switch on due to complication with the automatic changeover switch we will need to manually start the generator.Press the hand button   which will indicate a green light then press the green start button   to start the generatorAircon Activation This is only to be done by Dan, Dean and NauOnce we have determined the reason for the fault and the time frame to fix it, we have the option to activate different parts of the office aircon. This can only be done by Dan, Dean and Nau as they will need to determine the Voltage load on the Generator at the time. To re-activate the aircon:Isolate the Aircon circuit breakers in the switchboards2. Turn on the â€œGen Aircon bypassâ€ with the key (the key is located behind the security lights switchboard door).   3. Turn on the desired Aircon circuit breaker to start that unit.           Once the power has come back on the Automatic Generator/Mains transfer switch will countdown 5 minutes, then transfer back over to the mains power. The Generator will continue to run for another 5 minutes to cool down then it will shut down automatically and reset itself to Auto mode. Summary: This document explains how to complete the 'ODBC Driver Load' process within IT, so staff can follow the correct steps every time.
detail:
Informix Client SDK (ODBC Driver) Install

There are two versions of the driver, one for 32-bit applications and one for 64-bit applications.  The one to install depends on the bit count of the application that will be receiving the data, not on the PC s operating system.  Typical applications to receive Pronto data from Informix are Microsoft Excel, which tends to be 32-bit, and Microsoft SQL Server, which tends to be 64-bit.  It is possible and harmless to install both versions on the same PC so I suggest just installing both.

At three points in the process of installing and configuring the Informix Client SDK it will be necessary to have local administrative rights to the PC so likely IT need to run the applications as admin (right click and select). 

 To complete the configuration steps, it will also be necessary to have access to the Informix server on the default Pronto database port of 9088.  If you are installing the SDK on a remote site from the server, ensure you VPN connection is capable of connecting over this port.

32 and 64 bit versions are in this folder
Q:\Information Technology\Applications\Installs
As
installclientsdk64

and

installclientsdk
Step 1   Install the Client SDK software.
Start the installation program by right-clicking and choosing Run as Administrator.
/
You may have to provide an administrative user/password to enable this step.  Accept the warning that the program is about to make changes to your system and wait for the installer to unpack.
/
Just click Next on the introduction page.

/
Agree to the license terms and click Next.
/
Accept the default location or specify an alternative and click Next.

/
To avoid installing unnecessary programs and services, modify the Installation Features list as per the expanded screenshot above.  This feature list should be sufficient for all Excel ODBC and SQL Server OLE DB and ODBC requirements, and includes non-optional features.  The last option, IBM Informix OpenAdmin Tool, is a service and should always be excluded from the 32-bit install.  It is not present in the 64_bit install.  Click Next.

/
Review the feature list and click Install.

/
Wait for a few moments while the install completes& 

/
& and then ensure that the option for the IBM Data Server Driver Package is set to No and click Next.

/
When the installation is complete, you may be requested to restart your PC.  Whether or not you do so via the controls on this screen, click Done and make sure the system is restarted before any further steps in the configuration are performed.

Step 2   Configure the Informix Server Settings using Setnet32.
The application to configure the Pronto server s Informix details is called Setnet32, regardless of whether the 32-bit or 64-bit version of the program has been installed.  If both versions are installed, ensure that the program is run from the installation folder of both versions because they create different registry records and both will be required.
Run the Setnet32 application as administrator from the installation directory s bin folder.
/

Click the Server Information tab and enter the details for your server.  Most of the values are in common to all instances of Pronto, but the Hostname filed must contain either a valid hostname that will resolve to the IP address of the Pronto server, or the server s IP address.  Note that the Service Name, 9088, is actually the IP port on which the client SDK will communicate with the server. 

Our IP is 192.168.60.20 

/
Once the details have been entered, click Apply and answer yes to the prompt to create a new server record (this will only be possible if you run Setnet32 as administrator).  Click the Make Default Server button, and then OK to close the application.
Step 3   Create a Database Service Name entry in the ODBC Manager.
From Control Panel   Administrative Tools, run the correct bit count version of the ODBC Data Sources tool as administrator.  Again, the bit-count should match the bit-count of your data-destination application and the version of the Informix Client SDK you installed in Step 1.  If both 32-bit and 64-bit versions are installed, then this step will have to be completed for both 32-bit and 64-bit ODBC Data Sources.
/
Click the System DSN tab and then the Add button.  This will only be possible if the ODBC Data Source Administrator is run as a local administrator.  Choose the IBM INFORMIX ODBC DRIVER and click Finish.
/

Give the new Data Source a name (Pronto seems logical) and then click the Connection tab./

Most of the details will be automatically entered from the Setnet32 registry settings created in Step 2.  Complete the remaining details with the database name of the desired company (you can create separate entries for all the company databases you may wish to connect to, such as live and test) and add the username and password.  To avoid a long timeout, it is better to enter the username and password first, then choose the database from the now-available pulldown list.  Entering the database first causes a delay because it cannot be connected to without the credentials.

Our IP is 192.168.60.20
Database name is ffl
The person entering should know password
/
Check the connection with the Apply & Test Connection button.  If the test is successful then click Apply and OK to save the Data Source, which is now ready to use in the intended application.

Troubleshooting.

Installation and Configuration
The installation will fail if it is not run as administrator.
No data can be saved by the Setnet32 application if it is not run as administrator.
While it is possible to create a User DSN without administrative rights, it is preferable to run the DBC Data Source Administrator application as administrator and save the connection as a System DSN.

Connection
The user details entered in the ODBC Data Source should be a read-only Informix user.  Sometimes there is a single, shared user account created for ODBC use, other times individual users  Pronto accounts will be enabled for database connection.  This is done through the Pronto ProAdmin tool, by granting Connect permission to the user account for the required database(s) and granting the Select permission to the necessary views.  
If the connection test fails, ensure the following:
The database name is correct.
Check with the Pronto system administrator.
The user name and password are valid  
Sign into a Pronto session using the same credentials to validate the username and 	password.
The database connectivity is correct 
Pronto connection is valid but permission is denied when testing the ODBC connection.  Resolve this by correctly configuring the user s database connection and view selection permissions with in ProAdmin.
The connection is blocked  
Test that the Pronto server can be pinged.  If this is successful but the ODBC connection test still fails, ensure with the system administrator that the 9088 port is enabled through any VPN or firewall.

SQL Queries
Dates can cause difficulties because dates that have not been set in Pronto are stored in the Informix database as 31/12/1899, but most Microsoft applications cannot handle dates prior to 01/01/1900.  To get around this problem, date fields should be selected with a case statement to substitute values of 31/12/1899 with 01/01/1900
e.g. 	select case when to_char(invoice_date, '%d/%m/%Y') = '31/12/1899'
then to_date('01/01/1900', '%d/%m/%Y') 
else invoice_date 
end as invoice date, 
		& 
Field and view names can be found in Pronto ProMan, but take care to replace hyphens in field and view names with underscores.  Views should be used in queries, not tables, because table names change when Pronto is upgraded, but view names remain constant and so provided the selected fields have not changed, the query will require no maintenance due to Pronto upgrades.
/
E.g. View name is deb_master, table name is deb5mfw (w is a version suffix that changes on upgrade)
/
Field names should be taken from the DB Column Name column of the Layout screen, which is not always the same as the Filed Name column, and again hyphens should be replaced with underscore. E.g. bill_to, not bill-to.

Pronto Run-Down \ Run-Up Instructions
Ver 1.01   19/3/2021

Overview
The below instructions relate to the conversion of cable from the Pronto inventory code for 1 drum size to another code for the same cable but different drum size.
(eg Changing a drum (100 metres) of ML03/4.0BKG2/100 to 100m of ML03/4.0BKG2 so a customer can be supplied 50m)
It is only to be used where a fast conversion is needed for a sales order ie the physical conversion is expected to be done within a day.
Conversions of bulk quantities that may take multiple days to physically complete should continue to be completed by work orders through the Purchasing Dept. 
The conversion program makes the change immediately in Pronto, whereas the work order process will not record the completed stock until the process is finished, so to ensure that Pronto stocks and physical stocks normally agree, the work-order process should be used for jobs which will take longer time periods. 

Instructions for Run-Ups\Downs for Specific Orders
Select  Convert/Upgrade Items  from the below menu. If you don t have access, please see your HOD. Return over the Transaction Date field to accept today s date. 
If you receive a GL Transaction Date warning and not use to this, ask your supervisor.

/

As per the example below, you will see that the screen is split into 2 sections.
The left ( Original ) has the information of the stock item that will be taken from the shelf and the right hand side ( New ) the stock item that is being sent to the customer\remainder put back on the shelf.
  
/

In the following example we will assume that we are taking 100m of stock of ML03/4.0BKG2/100 and converting it into 100m of ML03/4.0BKG2 for a customer s order of 30m.
/
Left-hand side
From Warehouse: Enter the warehouse code for the stock being taken off the shelf (currently W1)
Item Code: Enter the Pronto product code for the stock being taken off the shelf
UOM: Return over the normal unit of measure for this item, or enter it if there is none (normally METR)
Qty: Enter the quantity that is to be converted.
Conv. Reason: Select STK RUND

Right-hand side
To Warehouse: Enter or  return to accept the warehouse code for the new stock item   normally the same as (a) (currently W1)
Item Code: Enter the Pronto product code for the stock being sold to the customer \ balance being returned to the shelf
NB. The brand code of the Pronto product codes entered on the left and right sides must be the same otherwise an error message will be displayed. If this happens, please see the Data & Systems Manager or Phil.
 
UOM: Return over the normal unit of measure for this item, or enter it if there is none (normally METR and should be the same as (c) )
Qty: Enter the quantity that is to be converted. 
NB It defaults to, and must be the same as that on the left (ie d) otherwise an error message will be shown.
Additional Cost: Return to accept 0.
Receiving Date: Return over the default to accept today s date
Enter over, or Mouse Click on the Ok button.
NB An error message may occur at any point if what you have specified would result in the cost of the two types of stock not being the same. If this occurs please see the Data & Systems Manager.

If you are transferring stock to a bulk cable code, a new lot number will need to be created in the next screen. 
Select Entry and then the system will give you the next Lot number which you will Return over to accept.
Return over the Location field
Enter the quantity that relates to that lot number
Return over the Receipt Date to accept today as the correct date
Repeat steps (a) to (d) if there is ever more than 1 lot number to create. 
When finished, press Escape to return to the screen menu bar
Select  Post  on the menu to update the Lot numbers and  Yes  to confirm on the next message window.

/

NB If the  Original  or From stock is a Lot Tracked Product, you will asked to select which lot numbers you want to draw the stock from.
If you have any issues with this step please see either your supervisor of the Data & Systems Manager.
A  Stock Conversion Order  (SCO) document will then print out on your designated printer, and, if relevant, a Lot number label   normally on the label printer in the Purchasing Office. An example is shown below.
The relevant sales order number should be written onto the SCO and the SCO and label attached to the front of the relevant picking slip.
When taking the documents to the warehouse, the SCO should be brought to the attention of the warehouse person responsible for completing the work.

General
The key difference with WMS is the use of RF gun to record most stock movements, and the critical element that all stock transactions in and out of warehouse locations must be recorded. This will facilitate greater visibility and accuracy of our stock.

EDI Processing \ General Sales Order Processing
EDI processing is largely the same as previous as the process has been changed to facilitate an automatic WMS upload and pick job release\print as soon as the sales order has been completed with the option of  Print Picking Slip  and  Print & Finish .

Please note that
More than 1 pick job may be generated for a sales order. 
Eg Cable that is lot tracked will appear on 1 pick job (which will be routed past the winders and scanned by the staff on winders when completed) while other product, including accessories, will be on another pick job and these will be scanned with the RF guns as they are picked off the shelves. 
The details for which lines are on which pick job and the status of those pick jobs may be viewed in  Detailed Order Processing  as shown below.

Sales order lines that are Notes will only print on the pick job that has the product immediately above under the note line.
Notes that need to be on all pick jobs (where there are more than 1) will either need to be entered under products of both types, or entered in the Delivery Instructions.

Detailed Order Processing

The status of the picking of a sales order can be seen in this screen

Selecting  Order  on the menu allows you to find a specific order
The main warehouse status values are as follows
Ready For Picking   order has been loaded to WMS but a pick slip has not been printed yet
Picking Slip Printed   the picking slip has been printed

 ZINVOICE  indicates stock already picked for an order
 LOST  indicates stock that ws in a location but cannot be found currently
 00000000  indicates stock that has been receipted
 TRISTAR  is for all stock stored at TRISTAR (NB movements to and from TRISTAR will in most instances automatically move stock on and off hold)

Background
this custom program has been written to transfer the contents of a stock location to another stock location in the same warehouse.

Moving Locations

Go to the Location move via datagrid function

/
�
�

At the bottom of the screen is a validate button - 
When the Validate button is clicked, the columns become colour coded: yellow is ok, red means there are errors related to the column. The detail of the error messages can be seen by clicking on the "Error" button.

/�

You can then press the update button to complete the transfer

below are the checks which are performed in the program:
Column "Whse":
Checks that the entered code is a valid warehouse
Column "From Location":
Checks that the entered code is a valid stock location for the entered warehouse
Checks that the entered code is not equal to "00000000" or "TRISTAR"
Column "To Location":
Checks that the entered code is a valid stock location for the entered warehouse
Checks that the entered code is not equal to "00000000" or "TRISTAR"
Checks that there is no inventory held in this stock location for any stock items stored in the "From Location"
�
If any of these checks don't pass, the transfer is aborted.
�
The tables which are updated by the program are the following ones:
stock-location
warehouse-stock-holding-file
sales-order-picking-location

Summary: This document explains how to complete the 'Pronto - Return Authorisation Process' process within IT, so staff can follow the correct steps every time.
detail:
Return Authorisation
The Return Authorisation (RMA) process is used to authorise warehouse staff to accept returned goods back into stock.
Return Authorisation Lifecycle
The following diagram demonstrates the lifecycle of a return authorisation sales order.

Creating a Return Authorisation (RMA) Order
A return authorisation order is used to create paperwork authorising the warehouse staff to accept returned goods back into stock. During entry of this order type, the contact name on the order must be entered or modified.
This order type is created by specifying an  R  order type using the Full Order Entry (SO�M001) function, as described below.
To create a return authorisation order
Select Sales Orders ( Full Order Entry (SO�M001).
Enter the customer name.
In the Type field, enter R.
In the Order No. field, press <Enter> to accept the next available order number.
The Return Authorisation screen is displayed.
 INCLUDEPICTURE  "C:\\Users\\grant\\AppData\\Local\\ Microsoft\\Windows\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Temporary Internet Files\\Content.Outlook\\LLCTLXOJ\\images\\return_authorisation1.png" \* MERGEFORMATINET 
In the Original Invoice No. field, enter the order against which the authorisation is being raised. Press F2 (Lookup Help) to display a list of all orders which have a suitable status for a return.
The details of the customer and the order amount are displayed. A menu is also displayed listing the following options:
Produce RMA from part of the original invoice.
Produce RMA from the entire original invoice.
Produce RMA WITH a tax-exempt number.
Enquire on the original invoice.
 INCLUDEPICTURE  "C:\\Users\\grant\\AppData\\Local\\ Microsoft\\Windows\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Temporary Internet Files\\Content.Outlook\\LLCTLXOJ\\images\\return_authorisation2.png" \* MERGEFORMATINET 
Select the required return authorisation option.
For the purposes of this guide, select the Produce RMA from part of the original invoice option.
/
 For more information on each of these options, see the Sales Orders online Help.
 
 If you produce a return from part of the original invoice, the lines for the original invoice are displayed.
Select the [Edit] mode and in the Action Type field, enter the type of return for the inventory.
For the purposes of this guide, select R   Return Item(s) to Stock.
Enter the quantity of items to be returned.
After you have completed the changes to the original invoice lines, select the [Finish] mode.
Enter the warehouse the goods are to be returned to.
You will be prompted for a reason the inventory is being returned.
Specify the reason code.
Press F2 (Lookup Help) to view the available return codes.
Finish the order.
At order conclusion it is possible to Finish (F), Print and Finish (P) or Edit (E) the order.  To print the order, you must be a Credit Release Officer and the order amount must be within your credit limit. 
If an order is Printed, the status will be set to RMA in Progress. If an order is Finished, the status is set to Return Authorisation.

Approving a Return Authorisation for Printing
Use the Approve RA for Printing (AR�M232) function to approve a sales order for which a return authorisation (RMA) has been requested.
All sales orders with the status of Return Authorisation are displayed in this screen for the attention and action of a Credit Release Officer.
To approve a return authorisation for printing
Select Sales Orders ( Order Edit / Maintenance ( Returns Management ( Approve RA for Printing (AR�M232).
The Sales Order Enquiry screen is displayed.
 INCLUDEPICTURE  "C:\\Users\\grant\\AppData\\Local\\ Microsoft\\Windows\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Temporary Internet Files\\Content.Outlook\\LLCTLXOJ\\images\\return_authorisation3.png" \* MERGEFORMATINET 
Highlight the order and then select the [Header] or [Lines] modes if you need to view the details of the order.
While the required order is highlighted, select the [Approve RMA For Printing] mode.
This changes the status of the order to RMA Approved For Printing and the order is removed from the screen.
Printing a Return Authorisation
After the return authorisation has been entered and approved for printing, the next step in the process is to print the return authorisation using the Invoice / Credit Note Print (SO�R100) function.
To print a return authorisation
Select Sales Orders ( Order Edit / Maintenance ( Returns Management ( Invoice / Credit Note Print (SO�R100).
The Invoice / Credit Note Print screen is displayed.
 INCLUDEPICTURE  "C:\\Users\\grant\\AppData\\Local\\ Microsoft\\Windows\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Temporary Internet Files\\Content.Outlook\\LLCTLXOJ\\images\\return_authorisation4.png" \* MERGEFORMATINET 
Enter the invoice date and specify the required range of territories, warehouses, warehouse groups, currencies and marketing codes.
Enter the number of copies to print.
Enter a message to be included in the print, if required.
In the Order Selection field, specify whether to print the return authorisation for:
A - All orders ready to print
M - Multiple orders
R - A range of orders
S - A set of orders.
The options that are available for selecting orders depend on the value specified in this field.
The status of the order now changes from RMA Print Approved to RMA In Progress.
Processing Authorised Returns into a Warehouse
Use the Receive RMA into Warehouse (SO�M182) function to process authorised returns into a warehouse. This function allows you to receive the goods into stock, edit the goods coming into stock and view the return authorisation order and its lines.
After the goods have been received into the warehouse, the status of the sales order is set to RMA Goods Received.
To process authorised returns into a warehouse
Select Sales Orders ( Order Edit / Maintenance ( Returns Management ( Receive RMA into Warehouse (SO�M182).
The Sales Order Enquiry screen is displayed. This screen shows the details of the Return Authorisation sales orders.
Select the required order.
Select the [Received RMA] mode.
Click Yes in the Confirmation prompt that is displayed.
Once the goods are received, the status changes from RMA in Progress to RMA Goods Received.
/
 You can also part receive an RMA if some goods are not in a returnable state. To do this, you would edit the return quantity which will split off an RMA child docket. This docket can be subsequently cancelled if no more goods will be returned.
 
 Approving an RMA
Use the Goods Received Confirm an RA (AR�M234) function to approve the RMA so that it can be converted into a credit note. After the credit has been authorised for goods that have been returned to the warehouse, a credit note is raised.
To approve an RMA
Select Accounts Receivable ( Admin/Credit Officer Functions ( Sales Return/Credit Note Menu ( Goods Received Confirm an RA (AR�M234).
The Sales Order Enquiry screen is displayed. This screen shows all orders which can be approved.
Highlight the required order and select the [Approve RMA] mode.
Click Yes in the Confirmation prompt that is displayed.
The Change RMA to a Credit Note screen is displayed.
 INCLUDEPICTURE  "C:\\Users\\grant\\AppData\\Local\\ Microsoft\\Windows\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\Windows\\Temporary Internet Files\\Content.Outlook\\LLCTLXOJ\\images\\return_authorisation5.png" \* MERGEFORMATINET 
In the Warehouse field, specify the warehouse to which the goods are to be returned.
Click OK.
The Credit Note Reason prompt is displayed.
In the Enter Reason Code field, specify the reason for the credit note.
Press F2 (Lookup Help) to access the  Credit Note Reasons   CN  code table and select from the available list.
The order now has a status of RMA Receipt Approved and you are returned to the Change RMA to a Credit Note screen.
The final step in the RMA process is to convert the RMA to a credit note. This can be done now by selecting the [Return Auth] mode in the Change RMA to a Credit Note screen, or at a later time using the instructions below.
Converting an RMA to Credit Note
The last step in the RMA process is to convert the RMA to a credit note. Use the Change an RMA to a Credit Note (SO�M019) function to create the credit note, as described below.
To convert an RMA to credit note
Select Accounts Receivable ( Admin/Credit Officer Functions ( Sales Return/Credit Note Menu ( Change an RMA to a Credit Note (SO�M019).
The Change RMA to a Credit Note screen is displayed.
In the Order Code field, enter the RMA order number.
The details of the order are displayed on screen.
Select the [Return Auth] mode.
The receiving warehouse can be changed if required.
Enter a reason code.
The RMA is now a credit note with a status of Credit Note Ready to Print.
Print the order and update.

Power BI Basic Usage
If you are set up with power BI (as a trial or as a proper licence) you can go to app.powerbi.com and you will see a screen like this. If you don t have a licence it will ask you to start a trial and then you will need to set it up   this process is simple but IT can assist.

/

It is customisable so this may change a bit as you use it
For most users you will just select workspaces on the side and then select the workspace called main reports.
/
You can now select the report group that you want   common reports will be Sales report (standard sales reports like in pronto yellowfin) and Budget Product (has the budgets at product level).
/
The index of these reports I kept here
Q:\Information Technology\Reporting\Standard reports\reports index.xlsx
In this case we have selected the sales report. Once in these reports groups you will see tabs on the side representing each report.
/

Reports starting with a number are HOD reports   these are generally locked down in terms of the dates and format because they need to be standard reports that refer to the previous period.
Reports without numbers tend to have many options
/
Date sliders change the date range you are looking at

/
Dropdowns and similar filters allow you to filter the entire report (all reports on the page usually) 
Common filters are site mate vs Firstflex, Topline (which is the high level categories (core/maxcab etc) customer groups (e.g. JA Russel cory s etc) and rep codes (SR, DT etc)
/
If you click on the report a filter pane will appear with more options for more complex filtering
/
Reports Index
The file located here
Q:\Information Technology\Reporting\Standard Reports\reports index.xlsx
Has an index of reports that looks like the below with a summary of each report in case you want to search for something specific
/
The main reports are 
 Budgets Product  which has a lot of reports that drill down to product level and has budgets for them
And 
 Sales reports  which has a lot of executive sales reports
Sales reps are likely to mostly use  Budgets product 
Reports worth looking at here are 
Customer Stock Sales
Category/Customer Sales Mgn
Category sales LM
OOS (out of stock)
Top Orders (last 60 days top orders)
Branch sales vs PCP (with drilldown)
And in the Sales reports
Revenue vs PCP and Budget selected
Sales order by day (this is usually used for monitoring yesterdays sales)
Example reports
BDM Budgets
In the sales report group
HYPERLINK "https://app.powerbi.com/groups/6f00c53a-2e67-423f-8f97-7efb89a943db/reports/b56f5d1a-7f40-4e15-b762-809e63cdc60f/ReportSectionb0d886fae0d33e4164cd?redirectedFromSignup=1&experience=power-bi"
Revenue vs PCP and budget shows you rep sales vs budget (and a comparable period)

/

 transaction date  is the period you want to look at. Here it is set from 1st April to change this either move the slider or click on the date and start typing it. Note that it will not let you enter a date after the end date in the start date or before the start date in the end date   so enter these in order.
Also note if your browser is set to American dates it will show up with the month and day the wrong way around   this can be fixed in the browser and It can fix this for you.
 Compare date  is the prior comparable period - usually the previous year.
Parameter   this is what shows up in the first column   currently the report is set to rep but other parameters that you could split the report by include regions and customer marketing groups.
Sales rep   if you are not showing the report with rep as a row you may want to have it as a filter
Zone   so you can filter by zone (which is a location based category)
Super group -  so you can filter by super group (which is a group of customers)
SiteMate vs firstflex   so you can filter out site mate if you want

This report returns too many columns to see on this screen so the slide bar lets you see the extra columns to the right   but the main sales vs budget numbers are on the left just after the rep name.
You can also use the more sophisticated filters on the side by clicking on the report then opening up the side bar click on any item to get the filter

/

/

Note clicking on any title allows you to sort by that field

Under budgets Product you can see another report called
Branch Meeting report
This report is mostly for if you are going to see a customer and need to know which of their products are selling well, or are out of stock or have had a large increase or decrease.
Customer Stock sales selected

/
Again there are date controls at the bottom and on the right are the controls like sitemate topline sob category and customer group.
If you filter for example by customer group you can see just the customers in a given customer group
/
You will see that the customer description filter has also changed to only include customers that are part of that group as most filters filter each other.

Out of Stock report
This report is mostly for if you are going to see a customer and need to know which of their products are out of stock (not just the ones that the customer orders lately) and the due dates for those items.
Report is called OOS and exists under budgets product
/
Sales Drill through Reports
In the Budgets product report group there is a report called Branch Sales vs PCP
This report is designed for you to be able to drill down by customer then by category similar to yellowfin s functionality for investigating trends.
Functionality
Multi Select
Certain reports will have filters that look like the below
Just clicking on say  Non Core  would deselect all the other options but if you hold down  Ctrl  it will allow you to select multiple items
/
Drill Through
Certain repots will have drill through functionality (and this can be set up for you if required on specific reports).
Right click on any row and a context menu will appear

/

If you select the appropriate thing to drill through to another report which will be filtered by that field (in this case customer). This duplicates the effect you would have clicking through in yellowfin.

/

Exporting
If you want to export data exactly as it appears you can export to PDF or PowerPoint, if you want it with a power bi powered PowerPoint report you can export to PowerPoint however to use this properly the recipient would need to have power bi.
To export to a pivot table you can use the excel function.
/
If you want to export just the data you use a different menu. Click on the report and 3 dots will appear 
/
Click on this then you can select export data from the menu
/
Now select the option you want 
/
and you should get a download of a excel file with your data that likely will need formatting
/

Filters
Also useful is the three lines that you see near those 3 dots
This will show you the filters applied to the current report

/

If you want to reset all the filters to the standard settings (in case you placed your own filters on it and want a fresh start) you can use the green icon with the arrow on it
/
Bookmarks

You can bookmark a report in a given state (i.e. specific filters etc) by using the bookmarks function
Which is the icon just to the right of the green arrow
You cha use add a personal bookmark

/

Since power BI is online you can also save links to the pages you want to see. In Firefox you could browse to a report page and press the favourite star in the top left corner of this image, this will allow you to add a link to the link menu also shown in the image below the address bar.

Display

If you need to see a report more clearly you can click on the square icon.
This will give you some options including full screen mode
/
And even closer view would be to click on the actual visual (eg graph or table ) you want to look at and when the little icons appears on the top right, you can select the square icon to the right of the 3 dots 
/
This gives you a full screen of the report called  focus mode  and there is a back to report button on the top left so you can go back to seeing any other reports that are on the page and any dropdowns for filters etc that exist.

Subscribing

If you want to receive a report each day in your email you can use the subscribe function
Select the 3 dots on the side of the report and select the option  Subscribe to report

Select create a subscription of it presents you with this screen
/
You will now get some options to schedule when you want to receive it
/
Once you have set these you can save your subscription.
Email will look something like this
/

Embed in PowerPoint
If you have some regular reports that you need to run you may want to embed in power point
Select Export   PowerPoint   embed live data

Select open in power point

This will mean that the power point has a live  version of the report that will refresh. You could add many reports and create a report format that you just refresh (and update any now powerBI related formatting required).
If you right click on the report in the power point there is a manual refresh option
/

Custom Reports 
If what you need doesn t exist or needs to be edited you can use the web interface for custom reports
If you select new report from the home page
/
You can select a data set to work with 
/
/
and create some default reports off it

From here you can edit these to an extent with the tools on the side adding fields

However in general if you want options on a report you can ask me and I will add it to the main report as a dropdown or list so it is easy to use.

Ad Hoc reports
Often you will want something a bit beyond what the report directly provides you   or you will want to not waste your time trying to construct it even if it is there. (eg Changing a drum (100 metres) of ML03/4.0BKG2/100 to 100m of ML03/4.0BKG2 so a customer can be supplied 50m)
It is only to be used where a fast conversion is needed for a sales order ie the physical conversion is expected to be done within a day.
Conversions of bulk quantities that may take multiple days to physically complete should continue to be completed by work orders through the Purchasing Dept. 
The conversion program makes the change immediately in Pronto, whereas the work order process will not record the completed stock until the process is finished, so to ensure that Pronto stocks and physical stocks normally agree, the work-order process should be used for jobs which will take longer time periods. 

Instructions for Run-Ups\Downs for Specific Orders
Select  Convert/Upgrade Items  from the below menu. If you don t have access, please see your HOD. Return over the Transaction Date field to accept today s date. 
If you receive a GL Transaction Date warning and not use to this, ask your supervisor.

/

As per the example below, you will see that the screen is split into 2 sections.
The left ( Original ) has the information of the stock item that will be taken from the shelf and the right hand side ( New ) the stock item that is being sent to the customer\remainder put back on the shelf.
  
/

In the following example we will assume that we are taking 100m of stock of ML03/4.0BKG2/100 and converting it into 100m of ML03/4.0BKG2 for a customer s order of 30m.
/
Left-hand side
From Warehouse: Enter the warehouse code for the stock being taken off the shelf (currently W1)
Item Code: Enter the Pronto product code for the stock being taken off the shelf
UOM: Return over the normal unit of measure for this item, or enter it if there is none (normally METR)
Qty: Enter the quantity that is to be converted.
Conv. Reason: Select STK RUND

Right-hand side
To Warehouse: Enter or  return to accept the warehouse code for the new stock item   normally the same as (a) (currently W1)
Item Code: Enter the Pronto product code for the stock being sold to the customer \ balance being returned to the shelf
NB. The brand code of the Pronto product codes entered on the left and right sides must be the same otherwise an error message will be displayed. If this happens, please see the Data & Systems Manager or Phil.
 
UOM: Return over the normal unit of measure for this item, or enter it if there is none (normally METR and should be the same as (c) )
Qty: Enter the quantity that is to be converted. 
NB It defaults to, and must be the same as that on the left (ie d) otherwise an error message will be shown.
Additional Cost: Return to accept 0.
Receiving Date: Return over the default to accept today s date
Enter over, or Mouse Click on the Ok button.
NB An error message may occur at any point if what you have specified would result in the cost of the two types of stock not being the same. If this occurs please see the Data & Systems Manager.

If you are transferring stock to a bulk cable code, a new lot number will need to be created in the next screen. 
Select Entry and then the system will give you the next Lot number which you will Return over to accept.
Return over the Location field
Enter the quantity that relates to that lot number
Return over the Receipt Date to accept today as the correct date
Repeat steps (a) to (d) if there is ever more than 1 lot number to create. 
When finished, press Escape to return to the screen menu bar
Select  Post  on the menu to update the Lot numbers and  Yes  to confirm on the next message window.

/

NB If the  Original  or From stock is a Lot Tracked Product, you will asked to select which lot numbers you want to draw the stock from.
If you have any issues with this step please see either your supervisor of the Data & Systems Manager.
A  Stock Conversion Order  (SCO) document will then print out on your designated printer, and, if relevant, a Lot number label   normally on the label printer in the Purchasing Office. An example is shown below.
The relevant sales order number should be written onto the SCO and the SCO and label attached to the front of the relevant picking slip.
When taking the documents to the warehouse, the SCO should be brought to the attention of the warehouse person responsible for completing the work.

Email Policy
Background Recently, an email containing sensitive data was accidentally sent outside the company. In light of this, we want to emphasize best practices for sending emails.
Email Groups:
If you regularly send emails to a group of people, please contact IT to create an email group. This will save you time and reduce the chance of errors.

Create Templates for Regular Communications:
For emails sent regularly, create templates. This ensures consistency and reduces the risk of missing or incorrect recipients.

Using the Address Book:
When selecting multiple recipients for an email, please use the address book in Outlook.
If you are sending emails to colleagues within our company, use the company-only address book for accurate and up-to-date contacts.
/

Manual Entry of Email Addresses:
If you enter email addresses manually, double-check each address to ensure accuracy. Consider the implications of this information leaking.

SAFE WORK PROCEDURE
 
 /
 
 This machine is only to be used by trained and authorized employees.
 
 
PERSONAL PROTECTION EQUIPMENT (PPE)
 
 Safety boots must be worn. 
 
 Hi Vis clothing must be worn at all times while working in the warehouse.
 
 
 Safety glasses and a face shield must be worn.
 
   Long and loose hair must be tied back.
 
 
 Ensure the correct gloves are worn e.g. if too loose, they could get caught.
 
 Close fitting/protective clothing must be worn. Remove strings hanging from pullovers/sweaters.
 
 
 Trainee to initial next to each instruction to confirm understanding.
 
 
POTENTIAL HAZARDS / SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
 
 Electrocution 
 Check lead for damage and current test tag before use
 
 
 Grinding wheel shattering / discharge of objects / flying debris
 Check for cracks / tightness
Stand aside till disk up to speed
Keep guard in place
Wear PPE   full face screen AND glasses / goggles and gloves
 
 
 Exposed grinding wheel - Injury or laceration to fingers
 Wear PPE gloves
 
 
 Dust inhalation
 Wear PPE dust mask if required
 
 
 Loud noise
 Wear PPE hearing protection
 
 
 Trainee to initial next to each instruction to confirm understanding.
 
 
LOCK OUT AND ISOLATION PROCEDURES When cleaning, repairing, maintaining, or changing parts of any 
machinery always follow the company s Lockout and Tag procedure SWP 21, prior to undertaking the cleaning etc. There are no exceptions to this company rule
 
 PRE-OPERATIONAL SAFETY CHECKS:
 
 The electrical certification tag is current.
 
 
 PPE safety glasses / googles / full face shield and gloves are available.
 
 
 The safety guards are in place and securely fastened.
 
 
 Check for general wear and tear. 
 
 
 Check the grinding wheel for cracks and chips.
 
 
 Check the rotation of the spindle for true even revolving of the wheel by spinning the wheel by hand. 
 
 
 The gap between the rest plate and the grinding wheel is no more than 4mm.
 
 
 Trainee to initial next to each instruction to confirm understanding.
 
 

OPERATING PROCEDURE:
 
 Make sure that no other person is in the immediate work area to avoid them being injured by flying objects.
 
 
 When starting the grinder stand to one side and then allow it to reach full speed before you start grinding. 
Do not use a wheel that vibrates. Immediately stop the work and check it. 
 
 
 Always grind on the face of the wheel and at the correct angle so you can see the grinding face. 
Move the object being ground back and forth across the grinding wheel or you will make a grove in the wheel.
 
 
 If the work is small, use vice grip or custom tool /material holder. Do not touch the work until it is cooled.
 
 
 When grinding be aware that the item will heat up. 
 
 
 When finished keep the work area clean for others to use. 
 
 
 If maintenance is required, the grinder is to be electrically isolated / locked out.
 
 
 Trainee to initial next to each instruction to confirm understanding.

 Compressed air

 Dust inhalation

 Adjust the pressure regulator to suit the particular work requirements. 
 
 
 Always check these pressures at regular intervals during normal operation. 
 
 
 Air hose connections must be secured and checked prior to being pressurized. 
 
 
 If portable, position the compressor unit in an area that will not disturb or obstruct the workshop environment.

 Never use the compressed air to clean down work benches, floors or dust from clothing.

 Always grind on the face of the wheel and at the correct angle so you can see the grinding face. 
Move the object being ground back and forth across the grinding wheel or you will make a grove in the wheel.
 
 
 If the work is small, use vice grip or custom tool /material holder. Do not touch the work until it is cooled.
 
 
 When grinding be aware that the item will heat up. 
 
 
 When finished keep the work area clean for others to use.

 PRE-OPERATIONAL SAFETY CHECKS:
 
 Conduct a task Risk assessment. Is a ladder / rolling stairs the safest, practical means of access for the task? Can the task be done another way?
 
 
 Always refer to the manufacturer s label for load ratings and other safety information. The rated capacity must be sufficient to accommodate the weight of the user and their load when using the ladder / rolling stairs. 
 
 
 Ensue the ladder / rolling stairs is appropriate for the task and is only used for the purpose for which it was designed.
 
 
 Inspect the area to ensure there are no surface, aerial or nearby hazards e.g. overhead power cables. 
 
 
 ALWAYS inspect the ladder / rolling stairs before each use to ensure there are no worn parts or damage before climbing.
Joints between steps and side rails are tight, all fittings/rivets are secure and moving parts operate freely.
Welds are intact.
Treads are free of mud, paint splatter, oil and grease. 
All components of the ladder / rolling stairs are intact including side rails, steps, treads, platform and the feet firmly attached and in sound condition. Check rolling stairs brake is operational.
Side rails and treads are free of excessive denting or other signs of wear. 
If any component is found to be worn or damaged immediately remove the ladder from service, tag it as  Out-of- Service  and notify the appropriate supervisor. FIX ANY FAULTS BEFORE USE.

SAFE LADDER USE:
 
 Step ladders should only be used for low risk, short duration work.
 
 
 Always face the ladder and use both hands on side rails.
 
 
 Climb slowly. 
 
 
 Maintain three points of contact at all times. 
 
 
 Only one person on a ladder at a time. 
 
 
 Only carry light materials and tools (up to 10 kg). 
 
 
 Keep both feet on the same rung or step throughout the task. 
 
 
 Avoid side-on working.

OPERATING PROCEDURE:
 
 Secure locking devices on ladders and engage brake on rolling stairs.
 
 
 Wear slip-resistant, closed-toe, sturdy footwear. Never wear sandals, high heels or flip-flops. Wear appropriate clothing (e.g. no loose or flapping clothing, and ensure clothing does not restrict movement when climbing). 
 
 
 DO NOT overreach when using the ladder. Unlock and fully collapse the step ladder and carry it parallel to the ground Hold the side rail in the middle of the ladder to balance the load. Get help to carry very long ladders.

 Year/s since initial training
 
 
 
 
 
 Conduct a task Risk assessment. Is a ladder / rolling stairs the safest, practical means of access for the task? Can the task be done another way?

POTENTIAL HAZARDS / SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
 
 Death, serious injury, damage to equipment & equipment in dangerous state
 Follow the Lockout and Tag Out procedure.

 
 
 Trainee to initial next to each instruction to confirm understanding.
 
 

If you have to physically access or enter any machine, equipment or control panel for the purposes of: 
Cleaning
Maintenance/ Servicing or 
Repairs
 
 Advise the manager responsible for the area where the lockout is to be actioned.
 
 
 Shut off the machinery or equipment. Make sure that all moving parts have come to a complete stop. Ensure that all power sources to the machine are disconnected or isolated e.g. electrical, hydraulic, air or steam. Also ensure that the act of shutting off equipment does not cause a hazard to other workers.
 
 
 Obtain and fill out a Locked Out tag in any situation that the machinery/vehicle MUST NOT be moved or operated. Ensure that all parts and attachments are secured against inadvertent movement.
 
 
 
Test the procedure to make sure it s effective and to verify that each energy source has been made inactive. (First ensure that all workers are in the clear and that no hazard will be created if not effective).
 
 
 Test - make sure zero energy is effective. (E.g. press start button on machines).
 
 
 Make sure there is no residual pressure in the lines, reservoirs, or accumulator feeding the cylinder. Bleed any residual pressure. Support any raised loads.
 
 
 Rule out inadvertent startup   consideration must be given to light beams, pressure sensors and computer controlled systems that may activate a machine automatically.
 
 
 Trainee to initial next to each instruction to confirm understanding.
 
 

Once cleaning / repairs completed
 
 The Locked Out tag originator can remove the tag.
 
 
 Before starting any machine / vehicle ensure; 
All tools have been removed, 
All guards have been fitted correctly and secured, 
All other employees are clear of the machine/equipment when restarting.
 
 
 If that person is off site and cannot be contacted or they are unable to return to the site, then the Operations & Technical Manager (Dan) or Product  Manager (Dean)  may remove a tag once they have completed a  Lock Removal Form

 Loading and unloading to be only conducted by trained and authorized employees.
 
 

 PERSONAL PROTECTION EQUIPMENT (PPE)
 
 Appropriate footwear must be worn. Shoe must be fully enclosed. 
 
 Hi Vis clothing must be worn at all times while working in the warehouse. 
 
 
 Trainee to initial next to each instruction to confirm understanding.
 
 

POTENTIAL HAZARDS / SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
 
 Serious injury
 Be aware of moving vehicles and pedestrians
 
 
 Product damage
 Correct forklift procedures to be followed
 
 
 Toppling of unstable / unsecure cargo
 Ensure cargo is safe to move
 
 
 Unsafe access to or egress from the truck / trailer
 Be aware of moving vehicles and pedestrians
 
 
 Trainee to initial next to each instruction to confirm understanding.
 
 

DOCUMENTATION:
 
 All loading and unloading documentation is to be accurately completed, legible at all times and filed in the correct place. 
 
 
 LOADING AND UNLOADING OPERATIONS:
 
 
 Employees have the right to cease work if they believe the loading or any other activities could place them or others in danger of injury or harm. If this occurs, they are to immediately contact their supervisor. 
 
 
 When trucks are being loaded or unloaded, the forklift driver has complete control and authority over the loading operation. The truck driver is responsible for managing and for opening the load. 
 
 
 

If the truck driver is not loading / unloading their own truck  they can either:
	"  Stay in the cab until the loading or unloading has been completed, or. 
	"  Stand in a safe zone in front of the cab or 
	"  Go to a safe zone area until instructed by the forklift driver to enter the loading space. 
	"  When closing the load, the driver can ask for assistance from the forklift operator but must provide clear 		instructions to the operator at all times. 
	"  Where there is an element of risk of a load shifting or toppling off the truck the driver is to stand near the 		cab area. 
	"  Where assistance is required from the forklift operator to (e.g. to SNAP the roof support pole into place) 		the driver must stand well clear of the forklift operation or in the safe zone, 
	"  The contractor/drivers are required to abide by any safety standards/rules and any other directions as 		set down by the company or their representatives (e.g. the forklift operators). 
 
 
 DAMAGED PRODUCT:
 
 Any product damaged during the loading or unloading operations must be reported to the manager for recording.
 
 
 REPORTING ACCIDENTS:
 
 All serous and other accidents, near miss incidents and minor accidents are to be reported using a Near Miss/ Incident/Accident Report & Investigation Form �as soon as possible.
